In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Surah al-Hajj

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling, and every pregnant female will deliver her burden, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they will not be intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah will be severe.﴾

In the opening of this noble surah, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, commands mankind to be mindful of Him, by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibitions. He explains to them that the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing, due to which nursing mothers will forget their infants and pregnant women will deliver their burdens, from the intensity of the terror and dread. And that people will appear in it as if they were intoxicated from the intensity of fear, though they will not be intoxicated from drinking wine. But its punishment is severe.

What Allah mentions here of the command to taqwa (God-consciousness, mindfulness of Allah) He mentions in many other places of His Book, such as His saying at the beginning of Surah an-Nisa: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and [be mindful of] the wombs﴾ [4:1]. Verses of this kind are very numerous.

What He explains here of the intensity of the horrors of the Hour and the magnitude of its convulsion, He explains in other places:
• such as His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, and the earth discharges its burdens, and man says, "What is wrong with it?" On that Day it will report its news﴾ [99:1–4];
• and His saying: ﴿And the earth and the mountains will be lifted and crushed with one blow﴾ [69:14];
• and His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with convulsion, and the mountains are crumbled to dust﴾ [56:4–5];
• and His saying: ﴿On the Day the quaking one will quake, followed by the successor. Hearts that Day will be palpitating, their eyes humbled﴾ [79:6–9];
• and His saying: ﴿Heavy it has become upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly﴾ [7:187].
And other verses indicating the magnitude of the horror of the Hour.

As for His saying in this noble verse, "fear your Lord" [22:1], the meaning of taqwa has already been clarified earlier with its Arabic evidences, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. Zalzalah (convulsion) is the intense shaking and disturbance, and the repetition of a thing's displacement from its place and its position; that is, the repeated deviation and shifting of it from its location. For when the earth is moved with an intense movement, everything upon it is violently convulsed.

His saying: ﴿On the Day you see it﴾ is in the accusative governed by ﴿tadhhalu﴾ (will forget), and the pronoun refers to the convulsion. The seeing is visual, because they see the convulsion of things with their eyes; this is the apparent meaning. It has also been said that it is from the cognitive sense of "ra'a" (to know).

His saying: ﴿every nursing mother will forget﴾: "every nursing mother" means every female who nurses her child. As for the form "murdi'ah" (nursing mother, with the feminine ending) rather than "murdi'" (without it), the reason is what is established in the science of Arabic grammar: that descriptive adjectives specific to females, if they are intended to express an action, take the feminine ending (tā' marbūṭah); and if they are intended to express a relation (nisbah), the feminine ending is removed. So if you say "huwa murḍi'" (she is a nurser), meaning that she has the quality of nursing, you strip it of the tā', as in the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Like you, pregnant I have approached, and nursing, and I distracted her from the one with amulets, the suckling child."

But if you say "huwa murḍi'ah" with the meaning that she performs the act of nursing, i.e., she puts the breast into the child's mouth, you say "murḍi'ah" with the tā', and from this is his saying:

"Like a nursing mother of others' children, who has lost her own children of her womb; this is error from the right course."

As he indicated with his words:

"Of the attributes specific to the female, none needs the tā' if it is for the sake of self-sufficiency, because the wording is explicit;
and where the meaning is that of an action, add the tā', as in 'she became a nursing mother of a newborn child.'"

As for what some of the Kufan grammarians claimed, that the mother of an infant is "murḍi'ah" with the tā', while the wet-nurse hired for suckling is "murḍi'" without the tā' — it is false. This was said by Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr (his commentary). He cited as evidence the line "like a nursing mother of others' children," for it establishes the tā' for someone other than the mother. Also the claim of the Kufans that a descriptive attribute specific to the female does not need the tā', because its purpose is to distinguish male from female, and an attribute specific to the female does not need such distinction since the male does not share it with her — this too is rejected, as Abu Hayyan also stated in al-Bahr, citing the usage of the Arabs: "murḍi'ah" (nursing), "ḥā'iḍah" (menstruating), "ṭāliqah" (divorced). The clearer position in this matter is what we have presented earlier: if the action is meant, the tā' is used; if the relation is meant, the tā' is dropped. An example of the tā' used for this meaning is the saying of al-A'sha:

"O our neighbor, separate from me, for you are divorced; so are the affairs of people: one departs and another arrives."

Al-Zamakhshari said in his tafsir of this noble verse: If you ask, why is it said "murḍi'ah" and not "murḍi'"?
I say: the murḍi'ah is the one who is in the state of nursing, putting her breast into the infant's mouth. And the murḍi' is the one whose habit it is to nurse, even if she is not actually engaged in nursing at the time of the description. So it is said "murḍi'ah," which indicates that when this terror overtakes her while she has put the suckling infant to her breast, she pulls it out of its mouth because of the bewilderment that befalls her.

His saying: ﴿of what she nursed﴾ — the apparent reading is that "mā" is a relative pronoun and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; that is, "what she nursed (it)," in accordance with the rule in the Khulasah (of Ibn Malik):

"Omission is common among them, clear,
in a connected returning pronoun, if it is governed by a verb or an adjective, like 'whom we hope, he will give.'"

Some scholars said: "mā" is a verbal-noun (masdariyyah); that is, "every nursing mother will forget her nursing."

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr: What strengthens its being a relative pronoun is the transitivity of "waḍaʿa" (to lay down, to deliver) to a direct object in His saying "ḥamlahā" (her burden), not to a verbal noun.

His saying: ﴿and every pregnant female will deliver her burden﴾: that is, every woman who has a pregnancy will deliver her fetus from the intensity of dread and horror. The word "ḥaml" with a fatḥah (ḥamal) means what is in the womb as a fetus, or on the top of a tree as fruit. ﴿And you will see people as intoxicated﴾: "sukārā" is the plural of "sakrān" (intoxicated); that is, whoever sees them will liken them to the intoxicated from the intensity of dread. ﴿But they will not be intoxicated﴾ from drink. ﴿But the punishment of Allah is severe﴾: and fear of it is what makes the one who sees them compare them to the intoxicated, because their minds will be gone from the intensity of fear, just as the mind of the drunkard is gone from wine.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: ﴿wa-tarā al-nāsa sakrā wa-mā hum bi-sakrā﴾, with a fatḥah on the sīn and sukūn on the kāf in both places, on the pattern fa'lā, with fatḥah then sukūn. The rest read "sukārā" with a ḍammah on the sīn and a fatḥah on the kāf followed by an alif, in both places as well. Both are plurals of "sakrān" in the strict sense. It has been said that "sakrā" with fatḥah then sukūn is the plural of "sakir" (with fatḥah then kasrah), meaning "sakrān," just as "zamin" is pluralized as "zamnā." This was said by Abu 'Ali al-Farisi, as Abu Hayyan transmitted it from him in al-Bahr. It has also been said that "sakrā" is a singular noun, but this is not correct.

The argument of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school) from this noble verse, that the non-existent is called a "thing," because He described the convulsion of the Hour as "a thing" in its state of non-existence before it comes into being — its refutation was explained in Surah Maryam, so there is no need to repeat it here.

Question

The scholars differed about the time of this convulsion mentioned here: is it after people rise from their graves on the day of their resurrection, to the open plains of the Resurrection; or is it an expression of the earth's convulsion before people rise from the graves?

A group of the people of knowledge said: this convulsion occurs at the end of the life of this world and the beginning of the states of the Hour. Among those who said this were 'Alqamah, al-Sha'bi, Ibrahim, 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, and Ibn Jurayj. This view has some merit from the standpoint of meaning, but nothing has been established from transmitted reports to support it; rather, what is established from transmission supports the opposite, which is the other view.

The proof of those who held this view is a marfu' hadith (one traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ) that has come with this, but it is weak and it is not permissible to argue by it.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said in his tafsir, explaining the evidence of those who said the convulsion mentioned is at the end of the world before the Day of Resurrection: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi' al-Madani, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet, and it was given to Israfil. He places it at his mouth, gazing with his eye toward the sky, watching for when he will be commanded." Abu Hurayrah said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the Trumpet?" He said: "A horn." He said: "And what is it like?" He said: "A great horn into which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of rising for the Lord of the worlds." Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands Israfil with the first blast: "Blow the blast of terror," so it terrifies the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth except whom Allah wills. Allah commands him and he makes it continue and prolongs it, and it does not slacken. This is what Allah means by: ﴿And these do not await but a single shout, for which there is no reversal﴾ [38:15]. Then Allah sets the mountains in motion so they become like mirages, and the earth is shaken with its inhabitants with a violent shaking. This is what Allah means by: ﴿On the Day the quaking one will quake, followed by the successor, hearts that Day will be palpitating﴾ [79:6–8]. The earth becomes like a ship sinking in the sea, struck by waves, capsized with its people, or like a lamp hanging from the Throne, swayed by the winds, so people sway on its back; nursing mothers forget, pregnant women deliver, children turn gray, and devils flee in terror until they reach the horizons, where the angels meet them and strike their faces. People turn their backs and call to one another. This is what Allah means by: ﴿The Day of mutual calling, the Day you turn back fleeing; for you there will be no protector from Allah. And whom Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾ [40:32–33]. While they are in that state, the earth splits from one end to the other, and they see a tremendous thing, and such distress overtakes them as only Allah knows. Then they look up to the sky, and it is like molten brass; then its sun is eclipsed, its moon is eclipsed, its stars are scattered, and then it is stripped away from them." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The dead know nothing of any of that." Abu Hurayrah said: "Then who is excluded when Allah says: ﴿So there will be terror for those in the heavens and those on the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾ [27:87]?" He said: "Those are the martyrs. The terror only reaches the living. Those are alive with their Lord, provided for. Allah protects them from the terror of that Day and gives them security. And it is the punishment of Allah which He sends upon the worst of His creation. And this is what He means by: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ up to His saying: ﴿but the punishment of Allah is severe﴾ [22:1–2]." End of quotation from him. The weakness of the chain of narration just mentioned is not hidden, as you see.

Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, before he cited the aforementioned chain, said the following: "This has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ in a manner similar to what these people said, in a report whose chain requires examination, and that is what Abu Kurayb narrated to us ... up to the end of the chain, as we quoted from him just above."

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this verse: "The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir has cited the basis of those who said that, in the hadith of the Trumpet, through the narration of Isma'il ibn Rafi', from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from a man of the Ansar, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said..." Then he related the hadith in a manner similar to what we mentioned, at length, then said: "This hadith has been narrated by al-Tabarani, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and others, in a very lengthy form."

The point of it is that it indicates this convulsion occurs before the Day of Resurrection, and it is attributed to "the Hour" because of its nearness to it, as one says "the portents of the Hour" and similar expressions. And Allah knows best. End of quotation from him. You have already learned the weakness of the chain just mentioned.

As for the argument of the other party, who say that the convulsion mentioned occurs on the Day of Resurrection after the resurrection from the graves, it is what has been established in the Sahih (the authentic collections) from the Prophet ﷺ through his explicit statement to that effect. And by this you will know [p. 259] that this view is the correct one, as is not hidden.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 1 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih, in the Book of Tafsir, in the chapter on His saying: ﴿And you see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾: "Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say on the Day of Resurrection: O Adam! He will say: Here I am at Your service, and I respond to Your call, and all good is in Your hands. He will say: Bring forth the group for the Fire from your offspring. He will say: O Lord, what is the group for the Fire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine, I think he said. Then pregnant women will drop their burdens, children will turn gray, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe.' That was difficult for the people, until their faces changed. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'From Gog and Magog there are nine hundred and ninety-nine, and from you there is one. You are among people like a single black hair on a white ox, or like a single white hair on a black ox. Indeed, I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed Allahu Akbar. Then he said: 'A third of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed Allahu Akbar. Then he said: 'Half of the people of Paradise.' So we exclaimed Allahu Akbar.'"

Abu Usamah said, from al-A'mash: ﴿And you see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated﴾ [22:2]... "intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated." End of quotation from Sahih al-Bukhari.

In it, the Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly states that the time when every pregnant woman drops her burden, and you see people as intoxicated but they are not intoxicated, is the Day of Resurrection, not the end of the worldly life.

Al-Bukhari also said in his Sahih, in the Book of Ar-Riqaq, in the chapter on: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾: "Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to me, Jarir narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: 'Allah says: O Adam! He says: Here I am at Your service, and all good is in Your hands. He says: Bring forth the group for the Fire. He says: What is the group for the Fire? He says: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. That is the time when the young will turn gray, every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe. This was hard on them, and they said: O Messenger of Allah, which of us is that man? He said: Rejoice, for from Gog and Magog there are a thousand, and from you there is one man. Then he said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise, so we praised Allah and exclaimed Allahu Akbar. Then he said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. Indeed, your likeness among the nations is like a single white hair on the hide of a black ox, or like a mark on the foreleg of a donkey.'" End of quotation from it. Its indication of the intended point is evident.

Al-Bukhari also said in his Sahih, in the Book of the Beginning of Creation, in the section on the narratives of the Prophets, in the chapter on Allah's saying: ﴿And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a way﴾ [18:83-84]: "Ishaq ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: 'Allah, Most High, says: O Adam! He says: Here I am at Your service, and all good is in Your hands. He says: Bring forth the group for the Fire. He says: What is the group for the Fire? He says: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. At that time the young will turn gray, every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe,'" up to the end of the hadith, similar to what has preceded.

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih, at the end of the Book of Faith (with a kasra on the hamza, i.e., Innama al-iman, as in the chapter title), in the chapter on explaining that this Ummah is half of the people of Paradise: "Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah al-Absi narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: O Adam! He says: Here I am at Your service, and all good is in Your hands. He says: Bring forth the group for the Fire. He says: What is the group for the Fire? He says: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. He says: That is the time when the young will turn gray, every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe,'" up to the end of the hadith, similar to what has preceded.

So the hadith of Abu Sa'id, which both Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) agreed upon, as you have seen, contains the explicit statement from the Prophet (ﷺ) that the time when every pregnant woman drops her burden, and you see people as intoxicated but not intoxicated, is after the rising from the graves, as you see. That is a sound and explicit text on the point in dispute.

If it is said: this text is problematic, because after the rising from the graves, females do not conceive and then drop their burden out of terror, nor do they nurse and then become distracted from what they nursed.

The answer to this is in two respects:

The first: what some scholars have mentioned, that whoever died pregnant will be raised pregnant, and so she drops her burden from the intensity of the terror and dread, and whoever died nursing will be raised likewise. But this requires evidence.

The second respect: that this is a metaphor for the intensity of the terror, like His saying: ﴿a Day that will make children grey-haired﴾ [73:17], and similar expressions of the well-known styles of the Arabic language.

Note: What the authentic hadiths we have mentioned some of indicate is subject to a question, namely: if the aforementioned convulsion is after the rising from the graves, then what is its meaning?

The answer: its meaning is the intensity of fear, terror and dread, because that is called zilzal (convulsion), as evidenced by His saying regarding what befell the Muslims on the Day of the Confederates of fear: ﴿When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes shifted and the hearts reached the throats, and you assumed about Allah assumptions. There the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking﴾ [33:10-11]; that is, it was a convulsion of fright and fear, not a convulsion of the earth's movement. His saying in this noble verse: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ indicates that the greatness of the terror on the Day of Resurrection is a clear reason for preparing for that terror through righteous deeds in the worldly life before the possibility becomes impossible. This is because, as we have stated several times, the emphatic kasra-marked inna indicates causation, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence in the manner of allusion and indication, and the manner of explicit text; that is: fear Allah, because before you are great terrors, from which there is no salvation except through His piety, Mighty and Exalted is He.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 3:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil﴾ ﴿It has been decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾. In this noble verse, He, glorified and exalted, mentions that some people dispute about Allah without knowledge; that is, they argue concerning Allah by attributing to Him what does not befit His majesty and perfection, like the one who claims that He has children and partners, and says that the Qur'an is "the fables of the ancients," and says that Allah cannot bring the decayed bones back to life. Examples are al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, al-'As ibn Wa'il, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and their likes among the unbelievers of Makkah, who disputed about Allah with that false dispute, without any basis of rational knowledge or transmitted knowledge. Along with their false disputing about Allah, they follow every rebellious devil; that is, every defiant, tyrannical one among the devils of mankind and jinn. ﴿It has been decreed for him﴾ [al-Hajj: 3]; that is, Allah has decreed by a decree of destiny and judgment that ﴿whoever takes him﴾ [al-Hajj: 3] as an ally; that is, everyone who becomes his ally, meaning the aforementioned rebellious devil, then ﴿he will mislead him﴾ from the path of Paradise to the Fire, and from the path of faith to disbelief, and ﴿guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾; that is, the intensely kindled Fire.

What He, glorified and exalted, mentions in this noble verse, that some of the ignorant, such as the unbelievers, dispute about [p. 262] Allah without knowledge, that is, they argue concerning Him without a basis of knowledge, He has explained in another place, such as His saying in this same surah: ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾ ﴿turning away [in arrogance] to mislead [others] from the way of Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 8–9], and His saying in Luqman: ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an illuminating Book﴾ ﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though Satan invites them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾ [Luqman: 20–21]. So His saying in the verse of Luqman, ﴿Even though Satan invites them to the punishment of the Blaze﴾, is like His saying in al-Hajj: ﴿It has been decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4]. This noble verse, which is His saying ﴿And among the people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge﴾ [al-Hajj: 3], and so on, includes within its threat and reproach: the people of innovation and misguidance, who turn away from the truth and follow falsehood, abandoning what Allah has sent down to His Messenger of clear truth, and following the sayings of the leaders of misguidance, who call to innovations, desires and opinions, to the extent that they have done such things. This is because the ruling is based on the generality of the wording, not on the specific cause.

Among the verses that indicate the unbelievers' disputing about Allah without knowledge is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop, and then he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–78]; and His saying at the beginning of al-Nahl: ﴿He created man from a sperm-drop, and then he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4]; and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth﴾ [al-Kahf: 56].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is void with their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment﴾ [al-Shura: 16]; and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They did not present this to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 58]; and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they should see every sign, they would not believe in it. Until, when they come to you, they dispute with you. Those who disbelieve say, "This is not but the fables of the former peoples"﴾ [al-An'am: 25]. The verses of this kind are many. As for what Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions in this noble verse, that He has decreed and judged that whoever takes Satan as an ally, Satan will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze, He has explained it in other places,

• such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾ [Fatir: 6],

• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Even though Satan invites them to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [Luqman: 21],

• and His saying, concerning His prophet and intimate friend Ibrahim: ﴿O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, and you will become an ally to Satan﴾ [Maryam: 45],

• and His saying [p. 263], may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan – indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing﴾ [al-Nur: 21].

And other verses besides these.

Know that there is understood from the implied meaning of this noble verse, namely the meaning of its opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafah, the implication by contrast): that whoever argues with knowledge, by the light of guidance from an illuminating Book, like this great Qur'an, in order to establish the truth and nullify falsehood through that good argument, then that is permissible and praiseworthy. This is because the implication of His saying ﴿without knowledge﴾ [al-Hajj: 3] is that if it is with knowledge, the matter is otherwise, and there is no following of Satan in that. This implied meaning is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best﴾ [al-Nahl: 125], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said in his tafsir: "This verse, by its implication, indicates the permissibility of true argument, because restricting the argument to the case of lacking knowledge of the proofs indicates that argument with knowledge is permissible. So the false argument is what is meant by His saying: ﴿They did not present this to you except for argument﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 58], and the true argument is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and argue with them in a way that is best﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]." End of his quote.

As for His saying in this verse: ﴿the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4], it means the punishment of the Fire, so al-Sa'ir is the Fire. May Allah protect us and our Muslim brothers from it. The apparent meaning is that the original form of al-Sa'ir is fa'il, in the sense of maf'ul (passive), from the Arab saying: sa'ara al-nar, yas'aruha (like manaʿa, yamnaʿu), meaning "he kindled it." Likewise, sa''araha with the doubled letter. On the dialect of doubling and of lightening, there are the two seven canonical readings in His saying: ﴿And when the Hellfire is ignited (su''irat)﴾ [al-Takwir: 12]. Among the Seven, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir in the narration of Ibn Dhakwan, and 'Asim in the narration of Hafs, read su''irat with the 'ayn doubled, and the rest read it with the 'ayn lightened. Among what has come in Arabic speech in the manner of the reading of Nafi', Ibn Dhakwan, and Hafs is the saying of one of the poets of al-Hamasah (the anthology of Abu Tammam):

She said to him one day, to make me hear, "Gently, for we have in our mother a need."

"And if she saw me in a kindled fire (musa''arah), then if she were able, she would add wood upon it."

For it is not hidden that His saying "musa''arah" is the passive participle of su''irat with doubling. By what we have mentioned, it becomes clear that the original form of al-Sa'ir is fa'il in the sense of the passive participle, meaning the fire that is kindled (musa''arah), that is, intensely lit, for by the intensity of its kindling its heat increases, seeking refuge with Allah from it and from everything that brings one close to it of speech and action.

There is a third dialect for this, though it is not in the Qur'an: "as'ara al-nar" in the form af'ala, meaning "he lit it."

[p. 264] His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾ [al-Hajj: 4] indicates that guidance, just as it is used for direction and pointing to good, is also used for pointing to evil, because He said ﴿and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze﴾. A parallel to this in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿So guide them to the path of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 23], and His saying: ﴿And We made them leaders who invite to the Fire﴾ [al-Qasas: 41], because the imam is one who is followed in his guidance and direction.

The use of guidance for misguidance, as we have mentioned, is a well-known Arabic style, and the speech of the rhetoricians on such things holds that it contains an "'inadiyyah" metaphor (a metaphor of contrariety, using a word in the opposite of its meaning). Their division of the 'inadiyyah into the sarcastic (tahakkumiyyah) and the playful (tamlihiyyah) is well known, as we have pointed out earlier. As for His saying: ﴿every rebellious devil﴾ [al-Hajj: 3], we have already clarified the meaning of "Satan" in Surat al-Hijr. Al-Marid and al-Marid in the Arabic language mean "defiant." One says: maruda al-rajulu (with a damma), yamrudu, so he is ma'rid and marid, when he is defiant. The apparent meaning is that the word "Satan" in this verse includes every defiant one who calls to the punishment of the Blaze and misleads from guidance, whether he is from the devils of the jinn or of mankind. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 5 (part 1 of 4):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, that We may make clear to you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as an infant, then [We let you reach] your maturity. And among you is one who is caused to die, and among you is one who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing [at all].﴾

This noble verse and the verses that follow it indicate that the disputation of the disbelievers mentioned in His saying, ﴿And among mankind is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge﴾, includes their disputation concerning the denial of the Resurrection, claiming that He, may He be glorified and exalted, is unable to revive decayed bones—exalted is He far above what they say, a great exaltation—as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And he presents for Us an example and forgets his creation; he says, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], and as His saying, may He be exalted, about them: ﴿And we are not to be resurrected﴾ [al-An'am: 29], and His saying: ﴿And we are not to be raised﴾ [ad-Dukhan: 35], and similar verses, as we mentioned earlier.

For this reason, may He be exalted, established great proofs for the resurrection of people from their graves, alive, to the plains of the Resurrection for reckoning and recompense. So He, may He be glorified and exalted, said: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. Whoever originated you with the first origination and created you from dust, there is no doubt that He is able to originate you and create you a second time, after your bones have decayed and mixed with the dust. For the restoration cannot be more difficult than the initiation of the act. This decisive proof of the power to resurrect—which is His, may He be exalted, creating the creatures the first time—mentioned here, has been clarified in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And it is He who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [ar-Rum: 27];
• and His saying: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79];
• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As We initiated the first creation, We will repeat it—a promise upon Us; indeed We will do it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104];
• and His saying: ﴿They will say, "Who will return us?" Say, "He who produced you the first time"﴾ [al-Isra': 51];
• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Were We fatigued by the first creation? Rather, they are in confusion about a new creation﴾ [Qaf: 15];
• and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you have already known the first creation, so will you not remember?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 62];
• and His saying: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Is not that [Being] Able to give life to the dead?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 37–40].

The verses of this kind are very many, and we have explained that at various places in this blessed Book, in Surat al-Baqarah, Surat an-Nahl, and others. And because of the strength of the indication of this proof mentioned for the resurrection, may He be glorified and exalted, made clear that whoever denies the resurrection has forgotten the first origination,
• as in His saying: ﴿And he presents for Us an example and forgets his creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], for if he truly remembered the first origination, he could not have denied the second origination;
• and as in His saying: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, shall I really be brought forth alive?" Does man not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?﴾ [Maryam: 66–67], for if he truly remembered that, he would not have denied the second creation;
• and His saying in this noble verse: ﴿If you are in doubt about the Resurrection﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]; i.e., in doubt that Allah resurrects the dead. Doubt (rayb) in the Qur'an is intended to mean uncertainty;
• and His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿then indeed We created you from dust﴾. We have already mentioned in Surat Ta-Ha that the verification regarding the meaning of His creating mankind from dust is that He created their father Adam from it, then created his spouse from him, then created them from the two of them through procreation, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam; He created him from dust﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 59].

Since their first origin was from dust, He applied to them the statement that He created them from dust, because the branches follow the root.

We have also clarified in Ta-Ha that the view of one who claims that the meaning of His creating them from dust is that He created them from drops, the drops come from foods, and the foods return to the dust, is not correct; and we clarified there the verses that indicate the invalidity of this view.

In this noble verse He mentioned the stages of human creation. He made clear that the beginning of his creation is from dust, as we have explained just above; so dust is the first stage.

The second stage is the drop (nutfah). In the language, nutfah is little water, and from it is the saying of the poet, who was a man of Banu Kilab:

"What harm would it be to you, if you informed me that I am ill, and your husband was absent one day, that you visit me?
And you place a drop in a cup, cold, and you dip your mouth in it, then you give me to drink."

His saying "and you place a drop" means: a little water in the cup. The intended meaning of "drop" in this noble verse is the drop of semen. We have already mentioned in Surat an-Nahl that the drop is composed of the water of the man and the water of the woman, contrary to one who claimed that it is from the man's water alone.

The third stage: the clinging clot ('alaqah), which is a piece of 'alaq, and 'alaq is congealed blood. So His saying ﴿then from a clinging clot﴾ means: a piece of congealed blood. From the usage of 'alaq for the said blood is the saying of Zuhayr:

"I have made her, twisted, her sides [strong], for two months, the 'alaq aborts from her wombs."

The fourth stage: the lump of flesh (mudghah), which is a small piece of flesh, the size of what the eater chews. From it is His saying ﷺ: "Indeed in the body there is a lump of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound," the hadith.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿formed and unformed﴾, its meaning has well-known views among the scholars, which we will mention here, Allah willing, and we will explain which the evidence shows to be preponderant.

Among them: that His saying ﴿formed and unformed﴾ is a description of the drop, and that "formed" is what was a complete creation, and "unformed" is what the wombs expelled of drops and cast out before it became a creation. This view is reported from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, transmitted by Ibn Jarir and others. The remoteness of this view is not hidden, because "formed" and "unformed" are attributes of the lump of flesh, as is evident.

Among them: that "formed" means complete, and "unformed" means incomplete. The meaning of this view, according to its proponent, is that Allah, may He be exalted, creates the lumps varying: some of them are complete in creation, free from defects, and some are the opposite; and the variation of people follows that variation in their creation, their forms, height, shortness, completeness, and deficiency.

Among those from whom this view is reported: Qatadah, as transmitted from him by Ibn Jarir and others; al-Razi attributed it to Qatadah and al-Dahhak. Among them: that "formed" means shaped as a human, and "unformed," i.e., not shaped as a human, like the miscarriage which is a lump of flesh, with no outline or form given to it. Among those from whom this view is reported: Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, and Abu al-'Aliyah, as Ibn Jarir al-Tabari transmitted from them.

Among them: that "formed" is what was born alive, and "unformed" is what was a miscarriage.

Among those from whom this view is reported: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. The author of ad-Durr al-Manthur said: Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it from him and authenticated it, and al-Qurtubi transmitted it from him, and he recited for this the poet's saying:

"Is weeping for an unformed one? Where then is prudence and modesty, woe to you?"

Abu Ja'far Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The most correct of the views on this matter is the view of one who said: "formed" means shaped into a complete creation, and "unformed" means a miscarriage before the completion of its creation; because "formed" and "unformed" are descriptions of the lump of flesh, and the drop, after becoming a lump of flesh, has nothing left until it becomes a sound creation except the shaping. That is what is meant by His saying ﴿formed and unformed﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]: a sound creation, and unformed: that the mother casts it as a lump without shaping, and the spirit is not breathed into it. End of quotation.

This view which Ibn Jarir chose has also been chosen by more than one of the people of knowledge.

The compiler of this work—may Allah pardon him and forgive him—says: This view which the eminent imam al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, chose, does not appear correct, and in the noble verse itself there is an indication that shows this: namely His saying, may He be glorified and exalted, at the beginning of the verse: ﴿then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. For according to the aforementioned view which al-Tabari chose, the meaning becomes: "then We created you from a formed lump, and We created you from an unformed lump." Addressing mankind with the claim that Allah created some of them from an unshaped lump contains, as you see, a contradiction; so understand.

If it is said: In the noble verse itself there is an indication that shows that what is meant by "unformed" is the miscarriage, because His saying ﴿And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term﴾ [al-Hajj: 5] implies that there is another category which Allah does not settle in the wombs until that specified term, namely the miscarriage.

The answer: It is not necessary to understand the miscarriage from the verse, because Allah settles in the wombs whom He wills to settle until a specified term; He may settle him six months, or nine, or more than that, as He wills.

As for the miscarriage: the verse has indicated that it is not intended, by the evidence of His saying ﴿then indeed We created you﴾; for the miscarriage which its mother casts dead, even after shaping and outlining, Allah did not create from it a single one of those addressed by His saying ﴿then indeed We created you from dust﴾ and so on. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an requires that each of the formed and the unformed is a kind from which some of those addressed in His saying ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop﴾ and so on are created.

By this you know that the most correct of the views on the verse is the view that contains no contradiction, because the Qur'an was revealed so that some of it confirms other parts, not so that some of it contradicts others. That is the view we previously cited from Qatadah and al-Dahhak, and al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf restricted himself to it and did not report any other.

It is that "formed" means complete, and "unformed" means incomplete.

Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: "Formed" (mukhallaqah) means made even and smooth, free from deficiency and defect; it is said: "He formed (khalaqa) the siwak and the stick" when he made it even and smoothed it, from their saying: "a smooth rock" (sakhrah khalqa'): when it is smooth. As if Allah, may He be exalted, creates the lumps varying; some of them are complete in creation, smooth, free from defects, and some are the opposite; and the variation of people follows that variation in their creation, their forms, height, shortness, completeness, and deficiency. End of quotation.

This meaning which al-Zamakhshari mentioned is well known in the speech of the Arabs. The Arabs say: "a hajar akhlaq," i.e., smooth, solid, unaffected by anything; and "sakhrah khal'a'" (a clear, smooth rock), i.e., there is no flaw in it, nor break. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"Time may leave in a firm, smooth rock a crack, and bring down from it the mountain goat, split [from its height]."

"Al-dahr" (time) in the verse is the subject of "yatruku" (leaves), and the object is "wahyan" (a crack). He means: the vicissitude of time may affect the solid stones free from breaks and flaws, so it breaks them and cracks them, and affects the mountain goats at the mountain summits, so it brings them down from their strongholds. From this also is the saying of Ibn Ahmar describing a horse, which the author of Lisan al-'Arab cited for the aforementioned meaning:

"With a tucked-up, swift horse, its back swift in pursuit of the prey, like a smooth rock of creation upon the plain, covered [with dust]."

His saying "kasafa al-khalifah" means: the horse's back mentioned is like a smooth rock with no break and no flaw, and this is an idafah of the qualified to its attribute. And an arrow that is mukhallaq is the smooth, even one.

The author, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, said: This view is, as it appears to me, the most correct of the opinions, because it accords with the language in which the Qur'an was revealed and because it is free from contradiction. And Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, knows best.

His saying, may He be glorified and exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿That We may make [it] clear to you﴾. That is, that We may make clear to you through this process, moving from one stage to another, the perfection of Our power to resurrect after death and over everything. For whoever is able to create humans from dust first, then from a drop of semen second, despite the incompatibility and difference between semen and dust, and is able to turn the drop into a clinging clot, despite the disparity and difference between them, and is able to turn the clot into a lump of flesh and the lump into bones, is undoubtedly able to restore what He originated of creation, as is clear.

His saying, "that We may make clear": the apparent reading is that it is connected to "We created you" in His saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾. That is: We created you in one creation after another, by the gradual stages mentioned, so that We may make clear to you Our power to resurrect and to do other things.

Al-Zamakhshari, explaining the reason for omitting the object of ﴿that We may make clear to you﴾, said the following text: The verb occurring without an object indicates that through these acts of His there becomes evident, from His power and knowledge, what memory cannot grasp and description cannot encompass. End of his quotation.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will for a specified term﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. That is: We cause to remain in the wombs of the mothers what We will to remain in them of embryos and fetuses for a specified term. That is, a known and determined term in Our knowledge, which is the time Allah has decreed for the delivery of the fetus. Fetuses differ in this according to what Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, wills. Sometimes the mother delivers it after six months, sometimes after nine, and sometimes after more than that. And whatever fetus Allah does not will to remain, the wombs reject and expel.

The reason for the nominative case of "wa-nuqirru" [and We cause to remain] is that the meaning is: "And We cause to remain..." It was not conjoined to His saying ﴿that We may make clear to you﴾, because it is not a cause of what precedes it. So the meaning is not: "We created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], so that We may cause to remain in the wombs what We will." By this, the nominative reading and the non-accusative reading become clear to you. As for the reading of whoever reads "wa-nuqirra" in the accusative, conjoining it to "li-nubayyina" [that We may make clear], it carries the meaning we rejected on the nominative reading. The meaning of the accusative reading is supported by His saying after it: ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Then We bring you out as a child﴾. That is: this happens after Allah turns the lump into bones, then clothes the bones with flesh, then brings that fetus into another creation, and brings it out from its mother's womb at the appointed time for its delivery, in the state of being a child, that is, a human infant, well-formed.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength [ashuddakum]﴾. That is: that you may reach the perfection of your strength, your intellect and your discernment, after being brought out from the bellies of your mothers in the utmost weakness and with no knowledge of anything.

We have already presented the views of the scholars on the meaning of ashudd [full strength], and whether it is a plural or a singular, together with some Arabic evidence, in Surat al-An'am, so that suffices here without repeating it.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this verse: ﴿And among you is one who is taken in death [yutawwafa]﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. That is: and among you, O people, is one who is taken in death before [reaching maturity], that is, before reaching his full strength. And among you is one who is granted a reprieve in his term, so he is allowed to live until he becomes decrepit. He is then returned, after his youth and his reaching the utmost of his strength, to the lowest age, which is senility, until he returns to his condition in childhood, in weakness and lack of knowledge.

We have explained the words of the scholars on "the lowest age" [arhal-umur] and the meaning of His saying ﴿so that he knows nothing after having known﴾ in Surat al-Nahl, so that suffices here without repeating it.

What He, may He be exalted, mentioned in this noble verse of the argument for His complete power to resurrect people after death and over everything, by moving the human from stage to stage, from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then from a clot, to the last of the stages mentioned, He mentioned in several places of His Book, explaining that it is among the decisive proofs of His power to resurrect and to do other things.

Among the verses in which this is mentioned without detailing those stages is His saying: ﴿No! Indeed We created them from that which they know﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 39]. And His saying: ﴿What is [the matter] with you that you do not attribute to Allah due greatness, when He has created you in stages?﴾ [Nuh: 13–14]. That is, stage after stage, as we have explained. And His saying: ﴿He created you from one soul, then made from it its mate, and sent down for you eight kinds of livestock. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; His is the dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6].

His saying in this verse of al-Zumar, ﴿in three darknesses﴾, means: the darkness of the abdomen, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta. Allah has assembled the bones of the human, some with others, clothed them with flesh, placed in them the veins and nerves, opened the channels of urine and feces, opened the eyes, ears and mouths, separated the fingers, and fastened their tips with nails, along with other wonders of His craftsmanship and marvels. All of this occurs in those three darknesses, without any need to split open the mother's abdomen and remove those darknesses.

Glorified is He, may He be exalted; how great is His station and how perfect is His power. He is the One who fashions you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Mighty, the Wise. And because of these wonders and marvels of His making, He, may He be exalted, said after drawing attention to them: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; His is the dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you turned away?﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. And among the verses in which He clarified those stages in detail is His saying: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a drop [of semen] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then made the clot into a lump, then made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. Then indeed you, after that, are to die. Then indeed you, on the Day of Resurrection, will be resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–16]. He, may He be exalted, mentioned those stages, omitting some of them, in His saying in Surat al-Mu'min: ﴿It is He who created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then from a clot, then He brings you out as a child, then [lets you reach] your full strength, then [lets you become] old men — and among you is one who is taken before that — and [lets you reach] an appointed term, and perhaps you will reason﴾ [Ghafir: 67].

• And His saying, may He be exalted, in al-Kahf: ﴿His companion said to him while he was conversing with him: Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a drop [of semen], then fashioned you into a man?﴾ [al-Kahf: 37].
• And His saying: ﴿He created man from a drop [of semen], and at once he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4].
• And His saying: ﴿Does man not see that We created him from a drop [of semen], and at once he is an open adversary?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77].
• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed We created man from a drop of mingled sperm﴾ [al-Insan: 2].
• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He created man from a clot﴾ [al-'Alaq: 2].
• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿From it We created you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55].

Besides these verses, and others, the authentic Sunnah has explained the period that the drop [of semen] remains before it becomes a clot, the period that the clot remains before it becomes a lump, and the period that the lump remains as a lump.

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us (ḥ). And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr al-Hamdani narrated to us, and the wording is his: My father and Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the truthful and the one whose truthfulness is attested, narrated to us: "Indeed, each one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days; then he is a clot for a similar period; then he is a lump for a similar period. Then an angel is sent, who breathes the spirit into him and is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or happy." The hadith.

In this authentic hadith there is the explicit statement of the Prophet ﷺ that the fetus remains forty days as a drop [of semen], then becomes a clot, and remains likewise forty days, then becomes a lump, and remains likewise forty days, then the spirit is breathed into it. So the breathing of the spirit occurs at the beginning of the fifth month of pregnancy.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, informing me: Sulayman al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: I heard Zayd ibn Wahb, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the truthful and the one whose truthfulness is attested, narrated to us, saying: "Indeed, each one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days, then a clot for a similar period, then he becomes a lump for a similar period. Then Allah sends an angel who is commanded with four: his provision, his term, and whether he is wretched or happy." The hadith. This narration in al-Bukhari omits the mention of the deed, which is mentioned in other well-known authentic narrations. We have already presented the aspect of the intended indication from the mentioned hadith, and Allah knows best.

In this noble verse there is a well-known question: it is said, what is the reason for the singular in His saying ﴿We bring you out as a child [tiflan]﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], although the meaning is "We bring you out as children [atfal]"? The scholars have given several answers to this question.

Among them is what al-Tabari ibn Jarir mentioned, saying: He used the singular "tifl" while it is an attribute of the plural, because it is a verbal noun like "'adl" [justice] and "zur" [falsehood], and others followed him in this.

Among them is the view of one who said: ﴿We bring you out as a child﴾ means: We bring out each one of you as a child. The lack of soundness of these two answers is not hidden. The author, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, said: What appears to me from the inductive study of the Arabic language in which the Qur'an was revealed is that among its styles is that a singular noun that is a generic noun, whose usage is frequent with the meaning of the plural, is used both indefinitely, as in this verse, and definitely with the article "al-" or with an annexed construction. Among its examples in the Qur'an, in the indefinite, is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river﴾ [al-Qamar: 54], meaning "and rivers," as evidenced by His saying: ﴿therein are rivers of water unchanging﴾.
• And His saying: ﴿and make us a leader [imaman] for the righteous﴾ [al-Furqan: 74], meaning "leaders."
• And His saying: ﴿And if they give you willingly some of it, [it is] a thing [nafsan]﴾ [al-Nisa': 4], meaning "things" [anfusan].
• And His saying: ﴿Being arrogant about it, conversing by night, disparaging﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 67], meaning "conversing" [samiran].
• And His saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any of them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 136], meaning "between them" [baynahum].
• And His saying: ﴿And excellent are those as companions [rafiqan]﴾ [al-Nisa': 69], meaning "companions" [rufaqa'].
• And His saying: ﴿And if you are in a state of janabah [junuban], then purify yourselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6], meaning "two in janabah" or "in janabah" [ajnaban].
• And His saying: ﴿And the angels, after that, are a supporter [zahir]﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], meaning "supporters" [mutazahirun].

Among examples of this with the indefinite in the speech of the Arabs is the saying of 'Aqil ibn 'Ulfah al-Murri:
"And the Banu Fazarah were the worst of paternal cousins, and I was to them like the worst of the brothers' sons [al-akhinā]."
meaning: "the worst of paternal cousins."

And the saying of Qa'nab ibn Umm Sahib:
"What is the matter with a people who are [true] friends [sadiq], yet have no religion, and no intellect when they are entrusted?"
meaning: "What is the matter with a people who are friends."

And the saying of Jarir:
"They set passion upon us, then shot our hearts with the eyes of enemies, while they are [female] friends [sadiq]."
meaning: "female friends" [sadiqat].

And the saying of another:
"By my life, if you were, despite the distance and separation, with you [feelings] like what is in me, indeed you are friends [sadiq]."

And the saying of another:
"O my blamers, do not increase reproach; indeed the blamers have no command over me [li bi-amir]."
That is: they are not commanders [umara'].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 5 (part 3 of 4):

Among its examples in the Qur'an, where the word is an annexed noun (mudaf) that has been omitted, is His saying, ﴿or what you hold the keys to, or your friends﴾ [al-Nur: 61], meaning: your friends. And His saying: ﴿let those who oppose His command beware﴾ [al-Nur: 63], meaning: His commands. And His saying: ﴿If you were to count the favour of Allah, you could never enumerate it﴾ [Ibrahim: 34], meaning: the favours of Allah. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, these are my guests﴾ [al-Hijr: 68], meaning: my guests. A parallel to this from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada al-Tamimi:

"Among them are the carcasses of the exhausted, whose bones are white, and whose hides are tough."

Meaning: and as for their hides, they are tough.

And the saying of another:

"Eat in part of your bellies, that you may abstain; for your time is a time of hunger."

Meaning: your bellies. Sibawayh cited this verse and the one before it in his book as evidence for what we have mentioned.

Among examples of this is the saying of al-ʿAbbas ibn Mirdas al-Sulami:

"We said: Submit, for we are your brothers, and the breasts have been cleared of rancour."

Meaning: we are your brothers (in the plural sense).

And the saying of Jarir:

"When our fathers and your father are counted, the ill-born mares are distinguished from the purebred ones."

Meaning: when our fathers and your fathers are counted. It is possible that these two verses are meant to show the sound plural (jamʿ al-taṣḥīḥ) of ab (father) and akh (brother), so that the original would be abūn and akhūn, and the nūn was dropped because of the annexation, so that it became like the singular form.

Among examples of the sound plural of akh is the verse of ʿAqil ibn ʿAlafa mentioned earlier, where he said in it: "He has ruined the sons of our brothers (akhīnā)." Among examples of the sound plural of ab is the saying of another:

"When they recognised our voices, they wept and ransomed us with our fathers (abīnā)."

Among examples of this in the Qur'an, where the word is defined with the article al-, is His saying: ﴿and you believe in the Book, all of it﴾ [Al ʿImran: 119], meaning: in the books, all of them, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Each believes in Allah, His angels, and His books﴾ [al-Baqara: 285] and so on,
• and His saying: ﴿Say: I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down﴾ [al-Shura: 15],
• and His saying: ﴿They will be rewarded with the lofty chamber (al-ghurfa) for their patience﴾ [al-Furqan: 75], meaning: the chambers (al-ghuraf), as evidenced by His saying: ﴿For them are chambers, above which are built chambers﴾ [al-Zumar: 20],
• and His saying: ﴿and they will be secure in the lofty chambers (al-ghurufat)﴾ [Saba: 37],
• and His saying: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels (al-malak) in ranks﴾ [al-Fajr: 22], meaning: the angels, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of cloud, with the angels?﴾ [al-Baqara: 210],
• and His saying: ﴿The multitude (al-jamʿ) will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45], meaning: the backs (al-adbar), as evidenced by His saying: ﴿do not turn your backs to them﴾ [al-Anfal: 15],
• and His saying: ﴿or the children (al-tifl) who have not yet attained awareness of women's private matters﴾ [al-Nur: 31], meaning: the children (al-atfal),
• and His saying: ﴿They are the enemy (al-ʿaduww), so beware of them﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4],
meaning: the enemies (al-aʿdaʾ). Similar examples are numerous in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs, and it is consistently found in the case of the qualifier being a verbal noun (naʿt bil-maṣdar), as has been mentioned many times before.

Among examples of this is the saying of Zuhayr:

"When a people quarrel, their chiefs say: they are approved among us, and they are just."

Meaning: they are just and approved.

* *

Issues related to this noble verse

The first issue: If the womb expels the sperm (nutfa) in its first stage before it becomes a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), then no ruling of the rulings on miscarriage applies to it, and there is no disagreement among the scholars about this.

* *

The second issue: If the sperm falls in its second stage, that is, when it is a clinging clot (ʿalaqa), meaning a solid piece of blood, there is no disagreement among the scholars that this clot is not prayed over, nor washed, nor shrouded, nor inherited from.

However, they differed concerning several other rulings from among its rulings.

From among them: if its fall was caused by a man striking the belly of the woman who expelled it, is a ghurra (an indemnity, originally a slave or its value) obligatory for it or not?

Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, held that whoever strikes the belly of a pregnant woman, and she expels her fetus as a clot, is liable for the blood-money of the clot as the liability for the foetus, so a ghurra is obligatory on him, or one-tenth of the blood-money of the mother.

In the Mudawwana: [it applies to] what is known to be a pregnancy, even if it is a lump of flesh (muḍgha), or a clot, or formed (muṣawwar).

The majority of the scholars held that the foetus carries no liability until the form of a human being appears in it. Among those who said this were the three Imams: Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī and Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on them all. The appearance of part of the form is, according to the more apparent view, like the appearance of all of it. They argued that it is not established that it is a pregnancy until it takes form. The Mālikīs said: the pregnancy can be recognised at the stage of the clot and what follows it, so their disagreement here is of the kind of disagreement over verifying the ground of a ruling (taḥqīq al-manāṭ).

From among them: if a woman is in ʿidda (the waiting period) following a divorce or death, and she was pregnant, and she expelled her pregnancy as a clot, does her ʿidda end by this or not?

The position of Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, is that her ʿidda ends by the expulsion of the mentioned clot. The Mālikīs argued: the mentioned clot is truly called a pregnancy, so it enters into the generality of His saying: ﴿And for those with child, their term is until they deliver their burden﴾ [al-Talaq: 4]. Ibn al-ʿArabi the Mālikī said: none of these rulings is attached to the foetus unless it is formed (mukhallaq), meaning shaped (muṣawwar). The majority of the scholars, including the three Imams and others, held that the expulsion of the clot does not end the ʿidda by it. They said: because it is a solid blood, and it is not established that it is a foetus.

From among them: if the mentioned clot is expelled by a slave-woman who is a concubine (surriyya) of her master, does she become an umm walad (a slave-mother) by the expulsion of that clot or not?

Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, and his companions held that she becomes an umm walad by the expulsion of that clot, because the clot is the beginning of a foetus. And because when the sperm became a clot, it is true of it that it was created as a clot after having been a sperm, so it enters into His saying: ﴿creating you in stages, one after another﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. Thus it is true of her that she delivered a foetus from her master, and so she becomes an umm walad by it. This is a narration from Aḥmad, and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī also said it.

The majority of the scholars, including the three Imams, held that she does not become an umm walad by her expulsion of the mentioned clot. We have already mentioned their reasoning for this.

* *

(p-276) The third issue: If the woman expels the sperm in its third stage, that is, when it is a lump of flesh (muḍgha), meaning a piece of meat, then there are four states concerning it:

The first: that some trace of the human form has appeared in that lump of flesh, such as the hand, the leg, the head and similar. In this case the ʿidda ends by it, a ghurra is obligatory for it, she becomes an umm walad by it, and there is no disagreement about this among those whose opinion is counted among the scholars.

The second state: that the mentioned lump shows no trace of human creation, but trustworthy experienced midwives testify that they saw in it a faint outline and form. The more apparent view in this state is that its ruling is like the ruling of the preceding one, because it has been made clear by the testimony of people of knowledge that this lump is a foetus, due to the hidden form they observed in it.

The third state: that the mentioned lump shows neither outline nor visible or hidden form, but trustworthy midwives testify that it is the beginning of the creation of a human being.

In this form the scholars differ. Some scholars said: her ʿidda does not end by it, she does not become an umm walad, and the one who struck her and caused its expulsion is not obliged to pay a ghurra.

Ibn Qudama said in al-Mughni: This is the apparent meaning of the words of al-Kharaqi and al-Shafiʿi, and the apparent meaning of what al-Athram transmitted from Imam Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him, and the apparent meaning of the words of al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbi, and all others who stipulated that some trace of human creation must be clear in it, because no trace of human creation has become clear in it, so it resembles the sperm and the clot.

Some scholars said: her ʿidda ends by the expulsion of the mentioned lump, she becomes an umm walad by it, and the ghurra is obligatory for it. This is a narration from Imam Aḥmad.

Some scholars said: her ʿidda does not end by it, but she becomes an umm walad by it.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears to me, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that if trustworthy, knowledgeable midwives testify that this lump is the beginning of a foetus, and that had it remained it would have developed into a human being, then her ʿidda ends by it, the slave-woman becomes an umm walad by it, and the ghurra is obligatory on the perpetrator by it. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

The fourth state: that the mentioned lump shows no outline, visible or hidden, and the midwives have not testified that it is the beginning of a human being. Its ruling is like the ruling of the clot, which we have already mentioned earlier in full.

* *

The fourth issue: If the woman expels her foetus dead after the form of a human being has been completed in it, then there is no disagreement among the scholars (p-277) that her ʿidda ends by its delivery, that she becomes an umm walad, and that a ghurra is obligatory for it. However, the scholars differed concerning the funeral prayer over it, washing it, and shrouding it. Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is not prayed over, nor washed, nor embalmed, nor named, nor inherited from, and it does not inherit, until it cries out (yastahill ṣārikhan) at birth. Its sneezing, suckling and urinating are of no account: if it sneezed, suckled or urinated, that would not make the funeral prayer obligatory over it according to Mālik's view, and this is the view of the majority of his companions. Al-Mazari said: its suckling establishes its life, so the funeral prayer and the other rulings become obligatory over it.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: The apparent correct position in this issue is that if its life is known, even by another means than crying out at birth, then the funeral prayer is to be performed over it. You know that the well-known position of Imam Mālik is that the criterion is crying out at birth. If it does not cry out at birth, its blood is washed off, it is wrapped in a cloth, and it is buried. The position of al-Shāfiʿī is that if it cries out at birth, or moves a movement that indicates life and then dies, the funeral prayer is performed over it and it inherits. If it neither cries out nor moves, then if it is not four months old, it is not prayed over, but it is wrapped in a cloth and buried. If it is four months old, there are two opinions: in the old (qadim) view he said it is prayed over, and in al-Umm he said it is not prayed over, and this is the more correct. Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions, Jābir ibn Zayd the Successor, al-Ḥakam, Ḥammād, al-Awzaʿi and Mālik, that if it does not cry out at birth it is not prayed over. From Ibn ʿUmar: it is prayed over even if it did not cry out. Ibn Sirin, Ibn al-Musayyab and Isḥāq also said this. End, transmitted through the quotation of al-Nawawi in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab. The position of Imam Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him, is that if it does not cry out at birth and does not move, then if it is four months old it is washed and prayed over; otherwise not. As for when it cries out at birth, there is no disagreement among them about the funeral prayer over it.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: Know that the disagreement of the Imams in this issue is of the kind of disagreement over verifying the ground of the ruling (taḥqīq al-manāṭ). The ground for ordering the funeral prayer over it is that it is known to have had a prior life, and the ground for not praying over it is that it is known to have had no prior life. Mālik and those who agreed with him held that if it cries out at birth, or its life lasts long enough, it is then known that it died after having lived, so it is washed and prayed over. They said: mere movement does not indicate life, because a slaughtered animal may move with a strong movement. They said: if it suckles, that does not indicate its life. They said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when the enemy of Allah stabbed him, was counted among the dead, so that if a person who was to inherit from him had died at that time, he would not have inherited from him. This is the view of Ibn al-Qasim. And if a man had killed ʿUmar at that time, he would not have been executed for it, because he was in the ruling of the dead, even though ʿUmar was at that time speaking and conscious (p-278) and giving instructions.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 5 (part 4 of 4):

As for those who disagreed with these scholars, they said: "We do not accept that. Every strong movement indicates life, and as long as the dead person is able to make a strong movement that indicates life, he is alive, and the rulings of life apply to him."

As for those who said that the fetus is washed if it falls after four months, they relied in this on the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim), which we cited in this discussion, in a form similar to what al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted. It indicates that after the third forty days the soul is breathed into it. The end of the third forty days is the end of four months. Thus the hadith indicates that the soul is breathed into it after the end of the four months. Breathing the soul into it at that time suggests that it died after having been alive, and God knows best.

* *

God the Exalted says: ﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs, swells, and produces every lovely kind of growth.﴾ This is another decisive proof of resurrection. His words "And you see" (Al-Hajj: 5) mean: O Prophet of God. It has also been said that it means: "And you see, O human addressed." This is visual seeing, which takes one object. Therefore His words "lifeless" (hamidah) is a state (hal) of "the earth," not a second object of "you see." His words "lifeless" mean: dry and barren, without any plant in it.

Some scholars said: "Hamidah" means: its traces of plant and crop have been effaced. They said: the root meaning of al-humud is effacement and obliteration. From this is the saying of al-A'sha, Maymun ibn Qays:

"Qatilah said: 'What ails your body, that you are so pale? I see your clothes worn out and decayed.'"

That is, "I see your clothes worn out and effaced."

﴿When We send down water upon it﴾ (Al-Hajj: 5) means: whether it is from rain, rivers, springs, or water-wheels (sawani). "It stirs" means: it moves with plants. Since the plants grow in it and are attached to it, their movement is as if it were the movement of the earth itself. So by this consideration it is described as stirring with plants. This is a well-known Arabic idiom.

Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit: "Its stirring is its loosening and the agitation of some of its parts for the sake of the emergence of plants." His words "and it swells" mean: it increases and rises. Some scholars said: "And it swells" means: it puffs up because of the emergence of plants. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: "And it swells" means: it multiplied the plants by the coming of the rain.

The one who wrote these notes (may God pardon him and forgive him) says: The root of the word from which "rabat" (swelled) derives is increase. The apparent meaning of the increase that occurs in the earth is that, since the plants are growing in it and attached to it, it becomes as if an increase had occurred in the earth itself. (p-279)

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said in his commentary on this noble verse: "Al-ihtizaz (stirring) is movement with joy. So one hardly says 'so-and-so was stirred by such-and-such' unless the matter is one of beauty and benefit." End of his quotation.

The root of al-ihtizaz is intense movement. From this is the saying:

"She sways when she stands, and when she walks she quivers, as the branch of the ben tree quivers in green leaves."

His words "and it produced" mean: God produced in it ﴿every kind﴾ (Al-Hajj: 5), that is, every kind of plants, crops, and fruits. "Lovely" means: beautiful. Beauty (bahjah) means loveliness. From this is His saying: ﴿So We caused gardens of delight to grow thereby﴾ (An-Naml: 60). One says: "bahuja" (with damma) "bahajah," so he is "bahij" when he is beautiful. Most of the seven readers recited "wa rabat," which comes from the saying "raba yarbu," when it grows and increases. From among the three additional readers, Abu Ja'far Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' recited "warabat" with a hamza after the ba', meaning "it rose." It seems to derive from al-rabi'ah or al-rabi'i, which is the lookout who stands high on something elevated to guard and protect the people.

From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"We sent a scout before that, one who is hidden, like a wolf of the ghada thicket that walks in the open and keeps watch."

What God the Majestic and Exalted indicated in this noble verse, that the revival of the earth after its death is a decisive proof of the power of the One who did that to revive people after their death, is because all of it is revival after death and creation after non-existence. He explained this in many verses. We have already mentioned in surah al-Baqarah and surah al-Nahl the frequency with which the Qur'an uses this proof for resurrection, and we mentioned the verses that indicate this, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is surely the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Powerful.﴾ (Fussilat: 39).
