It was also said that ﴿mu'jizin﴾ means those who follow the Prophet (ﷺ), and the meaning of that is that they ascribe them to incapacity, from their saying "'ajjazahu," with the doubled form, when he attributes to him the incapacity which is the opposite of resolve. They mean that they consider the Muslims foolish, without sound intellects, in that they committed an act that was not resolve or correct, namely following the religion of Islam in their view, as Allah, Exalted, said about their brothers the hypocrites ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, they are the foolish﴾ [al-Baqarah: 13], and His saying in this noble verse ﴿those who strive against Our verses﴾ [al-Hajj: 51].

Know first that "al-sa'y" (striving) is used for working on a matter either to corrupt it or to reform it. Among its use for corruption is His saying here ﴿those who strive against Our verses﴾, meaning they strove to nullify them and deny them by saying that they are sorcery, poetry, soothsaying, and "tales of the ancients," and the like. Among its use for striving in corruption also is His saying ﴿And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein﴾ [al-Baqarah: 205]. Among its use for working toward reform is His saying ﴿Indeed, this has been for you a reward, and your effort has been appreciated﴾ [al-Insan: 22], (p-284) and His saying ﴿But as for one who came to you striving, and he fears﴾ [‘Abasa: 8-9], and others besides these verses.

Among its use for both good and evil together is His saying ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾ up to His saying ﴿and his wealth will not avail him when he falls﴾ [al-Layl: 4-11]. This verse which he mentioned here in Surah al-Hajj, which is His saying ﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and generous provision, and those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [22: 50-51], has its meaning made clear in Surah Saba' in His saying ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and generous provision﴾ ﴿But those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, for those is a painful punishment of wretchedness﴾ [Sad: 4-5]. So the punishment of "painful wretchedness" mentioned in "Saba'" is the punishment of the Blazing Fire mentioned in al-Hajj.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 52 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he did recite (tamanna), Satan threw [some falsehood] into his recitation (umniyyah). But Allah abolishes what Satan throws in, then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. Concerning the meaning of His saying "tamanna" in this noble verse, the scholars have two well-known interpretations:

The first: that tamanna means "he recited and read," and from this is the saying of Hassan concerning Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him:

"He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of his night and its end, and met the death-decree of destiny."

And the saying of another:

"He recited the Book of Allah at the end of his night, reciting it as David recited the Psalms among the messengers."

So the meaning of tamanna in the two verses is "recited and read."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas, that he said concerning ﴿when he did recite, Satan threw into his recitation﴾: "When he spoke, Satan threw into his speech." That tamanna means "recited and read" is the view of most of the commentators.

The second view: that tamanna in the verse is from the well-known sense of "wishing," namely his wish for the Islam and obedience to Allah and His messengers of his community. The object of "threw" is omitted. So, on the basis that tamanna means "loved the faith of his community (p-285) and hung his hope upon that," the object of "threw" appears to be of the kind of whisperings and obstruction from the religion of Allah, so that what the Prophet ﷺ or the messenger wished for is not fulfilled.

The meaning of the throwing into his wish on this view is that Satan casts his whisperings and doubts in order to divert people from what the messenger or prophet wished for. Thus the throwing becomes as if it occurred within it, by obstructing its completion and preventing it.

And on the basis that tamanna means "recited," there are two estimates for the object of "threw":

One of them is of the same kind as the first: namely, Satan threw doubts and whisperings into the recitation of the Messenger ﷺ or the prophet, in order to divert people from following what the messenger or prophet recites and reads. On this estimate there is no difficulty.

As for the second estimate: it is that Satan threw into his wish, i.e., into his recitation, what is not part of it, so that the disbelievers would think it is part of it.

His saying ﴿then Allah abolishes what Satan throws in﴾ is taken as supporting evidence for this estimate.

Many of the commentators mentioned in the explanation of this verse the story of the Gharaniq (the "exalted cranes"). They said: the occasion of revelation of this noble verse is that the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah al-Najm in Makkah, and when he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [an-Najm 53:19-20], Satan threw upon his tongue: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for." When he reached the end of the surah, he prostrated, and the polytheists and the Muslims prostrated with him. The polytheists said: "He has not mentioned our gods with good before today." It spread among the people that the people of Makkah had embraced Islam because of their prostration with the Prophet ﷺ, until the emigrants returned from Abyssinia, thinking that their people had embraced Islam, and they found them upon their disbelief.

We have already mentioned in this blessed book that among the kinds of clarification it contains is that some scholars state a view concerning a verse, while there is in the verse an indication that proves that view false. We gave several examples of this. And this view which many of the commentators have asserted, namely that Satan threw onto the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ this great polytheism and blatant disbelief, which is their saying: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for," meaning al-Lat and al-Uzza and Manat, the third, the other, is without doubt false. Within the very context of the verses of "al-Najm" in which the alleged throwing of Satan occurred, there is a clear Qur'anic indication of the falsehood of this view, because the Prophet ﷺ recited, shortly after the place of the alleged throwing, the saying of Allah, exalted is He, concerning al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other: ﴿They are only names you have named them, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [an-Najm 53:23]. It is not reasonable that the Prophet ﷺ would revile their gods with this great reviling in Surah al-Najm, following upon his mention of them with the alleged good, without them becoming angry and not prostrating; because what counts is the final statement. Moreover, Qur'anic verses indicate the falsehood of this view, namely the verses showing that Allah did not give Satan authority over the Prophet ﷺ, and his brothers among the messengers, and their sincere followers, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [an-Nahl 16:99-100], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, over My servants you have no authority, except those who follow you of the deviators﴾ [al-Hijr 15:42], and His saying: ﴿And he had no authority over them, except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter﴾ [Saba' 34:21], and His saying: ﴿And I had no authority over you﴾ [Ibrahim 14:22]. And on the alleged view that Satan threw onto the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ that blatant disbelief, what authority could he have greater than that?

Among the verses indicating the falsehood of that alleged view is His saying concerning the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [an-Najm 53:3-4], and His saying: ﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every sinful liar﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 26:221-222], and His saying concerning the Great Qur'an: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr 15:9], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from One Wise and Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat 41:41-42]. These Qur'anic verses indicate the falsehood of the alleged view.

* *

Issue.

Know that the matter of the Gharaniq, along with its impossibility in the Shari'ah and the Qur'an's indication of its falsehood, has not been established through any sound channel fit for argument. A great number of the scholars of hadith have stated that it is not established, as is the correct position. The commentators narrate this story from Ibn Abbas through al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and it is known that al-Kalbi is abandoned (matruk). Al-Bazzar, may Allah have mercy on him, has made clear that it is not known through any channel that may be cited except the channel of Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, along with the doubt that occurred regarding its connection. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, despite his defense of it, acknowledged, regarding the establishment of this story, that all its chains are either broken (munqati') or weak, except the channel of Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

Having known this, know that the channel of Sa'id ibn Jubayr was not related with a connected chain by anyone except Umayyah ibn Khalid, and he, though he is trustworthy (thiqah), doubted its connection.

Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from the channel of Umayyah ibn Khalid, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, "as far as I reckon," then he related the story mentioned. Al-Bazzar said: it is not seen connected except through this isnad; Umayyah ibn Khalid alone transmitted it connected, and he is a trustworthy and well-known narrator. Al-Bazzar also said: it is only narrated through the channel of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and al-Kalbi is abandoned.

Thus it is concluded that the story of the Gharaniq was not transmitted connected except from this channel, whose narrator doubted the connection. It is known that what is of this kind is not used as evidence, due to the clear weakness of it. For this reason al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir that he did not find it traced back (musnadah) through any sound channel.

Al-Shawkani said concerning this story: "Nothing of this is sound, nor is it established by any means. And with its non-soundness, indeed its falsehood, the verifiers have rejected it by the Book of Allah:

• such as His saying: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:44], the verse,
• and His saying: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [an-Najm 53:3],
• and His saying: ﴿And if We had not made you firm, you would have almost inclined to them a little﴾ [al-Isra' 17:74].

So He negated even the approach to inclining, let alone inclining." Al-Shawkani then mentioned from al-Bazzar that it is not related through a connected isnad, and from al-Bayhaqi that he said: "It is not established from the standpoint of transmission." He also mentioned from the imam of imams, Ibn Khuzaymah, that this story is a fabrication of the zindiqs (heretics), and Ibn al-'Arabi al-Maliki, al-Fakhr al-Razi, and very many groups refuted it. The Prophet's ﷺ recitation of Surah al-Najm and the prostration of the polytheists is established in the Sahih, and nothing of the story of the Gharaniq is mentioned in it. And upon this sound view, that it is false, there is no difficulty.

As for the assumption that the story is established, as is the opinion of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, he said in Fath al-Bari:

"This story is established through three isnads, all of which meet the conditions of the sahih, and they are mursal reports, which those who accept mursal reports may use as evidence, and likewise those who do not accept them, because some of them reinforce others; for when the channels are many and their points of origin differ, that indicates that it has a basis. The scholars have many answers regarding this, the best and closest of which is: that the Prophet ﷺ used to recite the surah in measured recitation (tartil), with pauses interspersed. When he recited ﴿and Manat, the third, the other﴾ [an-Najm 53:20], Satan — may Allah curse him — said, imitating his voice: 'Those are the exalted cranes...' etc. So the polytheists thought the voice was his ﷺ, while he was innocent of that as the sun is innocent of touch." We have clarified this matter in our journey at length, and summarized it here, and in our book: "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab."

(p-288) The conclusion: the Qur'an indicates its falsehood, and it is not established through transmission; and the throwing upon his tongue ﷺ is impossible in the Shari'ah for the reason mentioned. Whoever affirms it attributes the uttering of that disbelief to Satan. It is thus clear that the Prophet's ﷺ utterance of that disbelief, even by mistake, is impossible in the Shari'ah; the Qur'an has indicated its falsehood, and it is definitely false in every case.

Al-Gharaniq: the white birds well known; its singular is gharnuq, like zunbur and firdaws, and there are other dialectal forms for it. They claimed that the idols rise to Allah like white birds and intercede with Him for their worshippers. May Allah disfigure them, how disbelieving they are!

And although we have mentioned that the saying ﴿then Allah abolishes what Satan throws in﴾ is taken as supporting evidence for the view of him who said that the omitted object of "threw" is estimated as: "Satan threw into his recitation what is not part of it," because the abolition here is linguistic abolition, meaning nullification and removal, from the expressions: "the sun abrogated the shade (nasakhat al-shams al-zill)," and "the wind obliterated the trace (nasakhat al-rih al-athar)" — this seems to indicate that Allah abolishes something Satan threw in which is not part of what the Messenger or Prophet recites. So what appears to us as correct, and that the Qur'an indicates it with clear indication, though those among the commentators who spoke on the verse did not notice it, is this: that what Satan throws into the recitation of the Prophet are doubts and whisperings preventing people from affirming and accepting it, such as his casting upon them that it is sorcery, or poetry, or the fables of the ancients, and that it is fabricated against Allah and not sent down from Him.

The evidence for this meaning is that Allah explained that the wisdom in the stated throwing is the testing of creation, for He said: ﴿so that He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Hajj 22:53], then He said: ﴿and that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so they believe in it and their hearts humble before Him﴾ [al-Hajj 22:54]. So His saying ﴿and that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth﴾, the verse, indicates that Satan throws upon them that what the Prophet recites is not true, so the wretched believe him, and it becomes a trial for them; and the believers who have been given knowledge disbelieve him, and know that it is the truth, not falsehood, as Satan claims to them in his throwing. This trial does not suit anything that Satan added from himself into the recitation. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

And upon this view, the meaning of "abolishing what Satan throws in" is its removal and nullification, and its having no effect upon the believers who have been given knowledge.

(p-289) [Commentary of al-Shinqiti, Adwa' al-Bayan, on surah 22, verse 52, part 2 of 3]

The meaning of "He makes His signs firm" (yuhkimu ayatihi) is that He perfects them in firmness, so that it becomes evident that they are a revelation sent down from Him in truth. The attempt of Satan to turn people away from them by the casting described above does not affect this. As for what He mentions here, that He empowers Satan so that he casts into the recitation of the Messenger and the Prophet a trial for people, so that those among them who believe are distinguished from the disbelievers,

(p-289) this test has been explained in many verses that we have already presented repeatedly, such as His saying: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve, so that those who were given the Scripture may become certain, and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wwills﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might know who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. And His saying: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾. That is, because it is a trial, as He said: ﴿Is that better as a hospitable provision, or the tree of zaqqum?﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire﴾ [al-Saffat: 62–64]. When this verse was revealed, they said, "The lie of Muhammad (ﷺ) has been exposed, because trees do not grow in dry ground, so how could a tree grow at the root of Hellfire?" And other verses besides these, as has been made clear repeatedly before. And Allah knows best.

The lam in His saying ﴿so that He may make what Satan casts a trial﴾ is, most apparently, connected to "cast" (alqa). That is, Satan cast into the wish (umniyyah) of the Messengers and Prophets, so that Allah would make that casting a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease. This differs from al-Hawfi, who said that it is connected to "He makes firm" (yuhkimu), and from Ibn 'Atiyyah, who said that it is connected to "abrogates" (yansakh). The meaning of its being a trial for them is that it is a cause of their persistence in misguidance and disbelief. We have already explained the meanings of "trial" (fitnah) in the Qur'an earlier, and we clarified that the root meaning of fitnah in the language is placing gold in fire so that by its smelting it becomes evident whether it is pure or counterfeit. In the Qur'an it is used with several meanings, among them: placing in fire. From this is His saying: ﴿The day they will be tried upon the Fire﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 13], meaning they will be burned by it. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who tormented the believing men and believing women﴾ [al-Buruj: 10], meaning they burned them in the trench of fire, according to the more apparent of the two interpretations. Among them also is testing (al-ikhtibar), which is the most common usage of it in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾ [al-Taghabun: 15]. And His saying: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial﴾ [al-Anbiya': 35]. And His saying: ﴿And that if they had remained on the path, We would have given them abundant water, that We might test them thereby﴾ [al-Jinn: 16–17]. Among them also is the outcome of a test when it is evil, such as disbelief and misguidance. Such as His saying: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193], meaning shirk, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and religion is for Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 193]. And His saying in al-Anfal: ﴿and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 39]. What clarifies this meaning is his saying (ﷺ): "I have been commanded to fight people until they testify that there is no god but Allah," the hadith, so the end-point in the hadith explains the end-point in the verse, (p-290) because the best thing by which the Qur'an is interpreted, after the Qur'an itself, is the Sunnah (the prophetic tradition). From this same meaning is His saying here: ﴿so that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾. The word fitnah has also come in one place with the meaning of proof (hujjah), namely His saying, exalted is He, in al-An'am: ﴿Then their fitnah was only that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [al-An'am: 23]. That is, their proof, as is apparent.

Know that "disease of the heart" (maraḍ al-qalb) in the Qur'an is used for two types:

The first: disease through hypocrisy, doubt and disbelief. From this is His saying concerning the hypocrites: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10]. And His saying here: ﴿so that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Hajj: 53], meaning disbelief and doubt.

The second: the use of "disease of the heart" for its inclination toward indecency and adultery. From this meaning is His saying: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest one in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32], meaning an inclination toward adultery and the like. The Arabs call the heart's concealment of evil matters "disease," and this is well known in their language. From it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"Guarding his private parts, content with piety, he is not one whose heart has disease in it."

And His saying here: ﴿and the hardened of heart﴾ [al-Hajj: 53]. We have explained in Surat al-Baqarah the Qur'anic verses that indicate the cause of the hardening of hearts, in discussing His saying: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that, so they became like stones or even harder﴾ [al-Baqarah: 74]. This verse of al-Hajj shows that what has become famous among the people of knowledge, namely that the Prophet is one to whom a revelation is sent but who is not commanded to convey it, and that the Messenger is the Prophet to whom a revelation is sent and who is commanded to convey what has been revealed to him, is not correct. This is because His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ [al-Hajj: 52] indicates that each of them is sent, and that despite this there is a distinction between them. Some scholars have inferred that the Prophet who is a Messenger is one to whom a Scripture and an independent law are sent down, together with the miracle by which his prophethood is established. And that the sent Prophet who is not a Messenger is one upon whom no Scripture was sent down, but who was revealed to call the people to the law of a Messenger before him, like the prophets of the Children of Israel, who were sent and commanded to act by what is in the Torah. This is as He explained by His saying: ﴿By it the prophets who submitted judge﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44]. And His saying in this verse: ﴿so that their hearts may humble themselves to Him﴾ [al-Hajj: 54], meaning that they may be humbled, submit, and be at peace.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan cast into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj: 52].

This noble verse indicates that every Messenger and every Prophet has Satan cast into his wish, that is, into his recitation, when he recites.

From this is the poet's saying about 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him:

"He wished for the Book of Allah on the first night and at its end, and met the death decreed by fate."

(p-346) And the other's saying:

"He wished for the Book of Allah on the last night, wishing as Dawud wished for the Psalms with ease."

The meaning of "wished" (tamanna) in the two verses is "recited" and "read." In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas, he said regarding ﴿when he wished, Satan cast into his wish﴾: when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech.

Some scholars said: "when he wished" means he loved something and desired it, so every Prophet wishes for the faith of his community, and Satan casts upon them insinuations and doubts, to turn them away from the way of Allah. And according to the view that "wished" means "read" and "recited," as the majority hold, the meaning of Satan's casting into his recitation is his casting of doubts and insinuations into what the Prophet recites, in order to turn people away from believing in it, or his casting into the recited text what is not part of it, so that the disbelievers would think it is part of it.

This verse does not contradict the verse that explicitly states that Satan has no authority over the believing servants of Allah who rely upon Him, and it is known that the best of them are the Prophets,

such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and upon their Lord they rely﴾ ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [al-Nahl: 99–100]. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them, except those who follow you of the misguided﴾ [al-Hijr: 42]. And His saying: ﴿So by Your might, I will mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them﴾ [Sad: 82–83]. And His saying: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

The reason the verses do not contradict one another is that the authority of Satan that is negated over the believing, trusting servants has two meanings among the scholars:

The first: that authority (sultan) means clear proof. On this view there is no problem, since Satan has no proof whatsoever, as he acknowledged in what Allah mentioned of him in His saying: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me﴾.

The second: that its meaning is that he has no power over them by causing them to commit a sin by which they perish without repenting of it. This does not conflict with what occurred from Adam and Eve and others, for that is a forgiven sin, since they repented from it. Therefore Satan's casting into the wish of the Prophet, whether we interpret it as recitation or as wishing for the faith of his community, does not involve any authority of Satan over the Prophet, but is rather of the kind of whispering and casting of doubts to turn people away from the truth, like His saying: ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear attractive to them and barred them from the way﴾ [al-Naml: 24].

If it is said: Many of the exegetes mentioned that the occasion of revelation of this noble verse is that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited Surat al-Najm in Makkah, and when he reached ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza﴾ ﴿and Manat, the third, the other﴾ [al-Najm: 19–20], Satan cast upon his tongue: "Those are the exalted cranes, and indeed their intercession is hoped for." When he reached the end of the surah, he prostrated, and the polytheists and the Muslims prostrated with him. The polytheists said: "He has not mentioned our gods with good before today." And it spread among the people that the people of Makkah had embraced Islam because of their prostration with the Prophet (ﷺ), until the emigrants returned from Abyssinia, thinking that their people had become Muslim, but they found them still upon their disbelief.

According to what many exegetes have mentioned, the authority of Satan reached a level by which he introduced into the Qur'an, on the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), manifest disbelief, as the apparent meaning of the alleged story requires.

The answer is that the story of the cranes, despite its impossibility by the law, has not been established through any sound channel fit for use as evidence. A large number of scholars have stated that it is not established, as we have explained fully in our journey.

The exegetes narrate this story from Ibn 'Abbas through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. It is known that al-Kalbi is abandoned (matruk) in narration.

Al-Bazzar has made clear that it is not known through any channel that may be cited except the channel of Abu Bishr from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, together with the doubt that arose regarding its connection.

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, although he defended the establishment of this story, acknowledged that all its chains are either disconnected or weak, except the channel of Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

When you know this, know that no one narrated it from the channel of Sa'id ibn Jubayr as connected except Umayyah ibn Khalid, and although he is trustworthy, he expressed doubt about its connection. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh recorded it from the channel of Umayyah ibn Khalid, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, "as far as I think," then he cited the story mentioned, and said: Al-Bazzar says it is not narrated as connected except by this chain, its connection was reported only by Umayyah ibn Khalid, and he is trustworthy and well known.

Al-Bazzar also said: It is only narrated through the channel of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Kalbi is (p-348) abandoned. So it is established that the story of the cranes has not come connected except through this channel whose narrator doubted the connection, and whatever is like this, its weakness is evident.

For this reason al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir that he had not seen it reported with a chain from a sound route. Al-'Allamah al-Shawkani said regarding this story: Nothing of this has been authenticated, nor has it been established by any route. And with its non-authenticity, indeed its falsehood, the scholars of verification have rejected it by the Book of Allah, such as His saying: ﴿And if he had attributed to Us some sayings﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44]; and His saying: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3]; and His saying: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would have almost inclined toward them﴾ [al-Isra': 74].

He negated approaching inclination to them, let alone actual inclination. Then al-Shawkani mentioned from al-Bazzar that it is not transmitted through an unbroken chain (isnad), and from al-Bayhaqi that he said: it is not established in terms of transmission.

It is also mentioned from the leader of the imams, Ibn Khuzaymah, that this story is a fabrication of the heretics (zanadiqa), and it was refuted by ʿIyad and Ibn al-ʿArabi, both Malikis, by al-Fakhr al-Razi, and by many other scholars.

Among the clearest Qur'anic proofs of its falsity is that the Prophet (ﷺ) afterwards recited in Surat an-Najm the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They are nothing but names which you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [an-Najm: 23]. So if we assume he said, "Those are the exalted cranes," and then retracted it with His words, "They are nothing but names which you have named," how would the polytheists rejoice after this retraction and this complete condemnation of their idols, that they are names without referents? This is the latter point.

His recitation (ﷺ) of Surat an-Najm in Makkah and the polytheists' prostration are established in the Sahih, and nothing of the story of the cranes is mentioned in those reports. On the view that the story is false, there is no difficulty.

As for the view that the story is established, which is the opinion of al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, he said in Fath al-Bari that this story is established through three chains, all of which meet the conditions of the Sahih. They are mursal reports (reports in which the Companion is omitted from the chain), which those who accept mursal reports can use as evidence, and those who do not accept them also accept, because some of them reinforce others. When the routes are numerous and their sources differ, that indicates the story has a basis.

The scholars gave many answers to this. Among the best and closest is that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite the surah in a measured manner, with pauses between its parts. When he recited, ﴿And Manat, the third, the other﴾, Satan, may Allah curse him, imitated the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Those are the exalted cranes," and so on. So the polytheists thought the voice was the voice of the Prophet (ﷺ), while he was innocent of that, as the sun is innocent of touch.

We have explained this matter thoroughly in our journey (rihla), so we have abbreviated it here. It is clear that there is no contradiction among the verses, and Allah knows best.

(p-291) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the disbelievers will not cease to be in doubt (mirya), that is, in uncertainty and suspicion, concerning it, that is, concerning this Great Qur'an, as is the apparent meaning. Ibn Jarir chose this view, and it is the saying of Ibn Juraij, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it from them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: "in doubt about it" means in doubt about what Satan cast (into the recitation). Allah also mentions in this verse that they will continue in this state until the Hour (al-sa'ah), that is, the Resurrection, comes upon them suddenly, that is, unexpectedly, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.

Mujahid related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the barren day mentioned is the Day of Badr. Likewise Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and others said so. Ibn Jarir chose this view, as Ibn Kathir transmitted it from them in his tafsir. Then he said: Mujahid and Ikrimah, in one narration from them, said: it is the Day of Resurrection, which has no night. Likewise al-Dahhak and al-Hasan al-Basri said. Then he said: This view is the correct one, although the Day of Badr is among the things they were threatened with. End of quote from Ibn Kathir, the point of relevance.

We have mentioned many times that we explained in the introduction to this blessed book that among the kinds of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars state an opinion about a verse while there is within the verse an indication (qarinah) showing that this opinion is not correct. We mentioned many examples of this. By it you know that the Qur'anic indication here shows that the barren day means the Day of Resurrection, not the Day of Badr. This is because He, exalted is He, followed the mention of the barren day with His saying: ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them﴾ [al-Hajj: 56], and that is the Day of Resurrection. His saying "on that Day" means the day when the Hour comes upon them, or the barren punishment comes upon them, and all of that is the Day of Resurrection. It is thus clear that the barren day is the Day of Resurrection, even though the Day of Badr was barren for the disbelievers, since no good came to them in it, and what befell them befell them.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 56:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that dominion on the Day of Resurrection belongs to Him, although dominion in this world also belongs to Him, since in this world there are kings among the created beings. On the Day of Resurrection, however, the name "King" will belong to none but Allah, majestic and exalted, alone. What He mentions in this noble verse, that dominion on the Day of Resurrection belongs to Him, and it is known that the King is the one who has judgment among the creatures, He has clarified in other places:

• Such as His saying, ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4].

• And His saying, ﴿The dominion that Day is the true dominion of the Most Merciful﴾, and the verse continues [al-Furqan: 26].

• And His saying (p-292) ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

• And His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And His is the dominion on the Day the Trumpet is blown﴾, and the verse continues [al-An'am: 73],

and other verses besides these.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in gardens of bliss﴾ ﴿And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, for them will be a humiliating punishment﴾. The admission of those who believed and did righteous deeds into Paradise, mentioned here, and the fact that the disbelievers who denied the signs of Allah will have a humiliating punishment, includes a detailed explanation of Allah's judgment between them in His saying "He will judge between them" [al-Hajj: 56]. As for what He mentions here of promise and threat, we have already clarified the verses indicating its meaning many times over, in abundance, so that this makes it unnecessary to repeat it here.

The Most High said: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah, then were killed or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ In this verse, the Most High mentioned that the believers who emigrated in the way of Allah and then were killed, by being slain by the disbelievers in jihad (because this is the most common case among those of them who were killed), or who died in their beds, natural deaths outside of jihad, that He, the Most High, swore that He would surely provide for them a good provision, and that He is the best of providers. What this noble verse includes of the matters we have mentioned has been explained in other places in the Qur'an.

As for those who were killed in the way of Allah, Allah, the Most High, has made clear that He provides for them a good provision, and that is in His saying, the Most High: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Al 'Imran: 169]. There is no doubt that what they are provided with is a good provision. As for those who died while fighting, those mentioned in His saying here, "or died," Allah has said concerning them: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah﴾ [An-Nisa': 100]. There is no doubt that whoever has his reward incumbent upon Allah, Allah provides him with a good provision, as is well known.

And the ahadith indicating this are numerous.

Ibn Kathir has mentioned a portion of them in his tafsir of this verse, and Allah knows best. As for His saying in this verse, ﴿then were killed﴾ (thumma qutiluu), Ibn 'Amir read it with the taa' doubled (qutilu, with tashdid), while the rest read it with the taa' lightened (qutiluu, with takhfif).

The Exalted said: ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great.﴾

(p-293) Many of the exegetes have mentioned that the demonstrative in His words "That" refers back to the support of the wronged among His believing servants, mentioned before it in His words ﴿That, and whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, and then is transgressed against, Allah will surely support him﴾ [al-Hajj: 60], meaning: that aforementioned support occurs because He is Able and does not fail to support whom He wills, and among the signs of His overwhelming power is that He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night; or it occurs because He is the Creator of the night and the day and the One who alternates them, so nothing that takes place within them at the hands of His servants of good and evil, of oppression and victory, is hidden from Him, and because He is Hearing of what they say and Seeing of what they do. That is, this attribute of creating the day and the night, and encompassing what takes place within them, and encompassing every word and deed, is because Allah is the Truth, meaning: the One whose divinity and entitlement to worship is established, Him alone, and that everything that is claimed to be a god besides Him is falsehood and disbelief, and a burden upon its adherent; and because He, may He be exalted and high, is the Most High, the Great, who is higher than everything, greater and mightier. Glorified and exalted is He, with a great exaltation.

He, the Exalted, has indicated the first of what we mentioned by His words ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day﴾ (the verse) [al-Hajj: 61], and the last of it by His words ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ (the verse) [al-Hajj: 62].

What appears more correct to me is that the demonstrative in His words "That" refers to something more general than the support of the oppressed, and that it refers to His words ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them﴾ [al-Hajj: 56], to what He mentioned of the support of the oppressed; that is: that aforementioned matter, namely that dominion belongs to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection, and that He alone is the Judge among His creation, and that He admits the righteous into Gardens of Bliss and punishes those who disbelieve with a humiliating punishment, and supports whoever among His believing servants is wronged, because He is Able over everything. Among the evidences of this is that He causes the night to enter into the day, to the end of what we have mentioned. This which He described Himself with here, of the attributes of perfection and majesty, He mentioned in other places, such as His words in Surat Luqman, clarifying that whoever is described by these attributes is able to revive the dead and create people: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ [Luqman: 28].

Then He gave evidence of His power over creation and resurrection, saying: ﴿Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term, and that Allah is Acquainted with what you do?﴾ ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Great﴾ [Luqman: 29–30]. These attributes, which indicate His perfect power, are cited as evidence of His power in "al-Hajj" and in "Luqman." The entering of each of the night and the day into the other has two meanings:

(p-294) The first, which is the view of most, is that the entering of each of them into the other is by the insertion of a part of one into the other; and by this the day lengthens in summer, because a portion of the night has entered into it, and the night lengthens in winter, because a portion of the day has entered into it. This is among the evidences of His complete power.

The second meaning: the entering of one of them into the other is the bringing about of the darkness of this one in the place of the light of that one, through the setting of the sun, and the light of that one in the place of the darkness of this one, as a closed house is lit by a lamp and darkened by its loss. Az-Zamakhshari mentioned this view, and it seems he inclines towards it; but the first is more apparent and more widely held. And Allah knows best.

His words, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [al-Hajj: 62] are read by Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i as "yad'una" with the lower-dot ya' (third person), and read by the rest with the upper-dot ta' of address (second person).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green?  Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted [with all things].﴾ The apparent meaning is that "tara" (ترَ) here is from ra'a (رأى) meaning "ʿalima" (عَلِمَ, to know); for the sending down of rain, although it is witnessed by the eye, the fact that it is Allah who sent it down is perceived only by knowledge, not by sight. So the seeing here is, in verification, a seeing of knowledge.

The meaning, then, is: "Do you not know that Allah sends down water from the sky, so that the earth becomes green," that is, possessed of greenery, because of the vegetation that Allah causes to grow in it as a result of His sending down water from the sky. This is one of His signs and proofs of His power to resurrect, as we have explained many times.

This meaning mentioned here, namely that the growth of the earth's vegetation through the sending down of water is one of His signs indicating His perfect power, has been clarified in many verses:

• As in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells.﴾ [Fussilat: 39], then He explained that this is among the proofs of resurrection

• by His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who has revived it is the Reviver of the dead.﴾ [Fussilat: 39]

• And as in His saying: ﴿So look at the effects of Allah's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 50], then He explained that this is among the proofs of resurrection

• by His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is the Reviver of the dead, and He is over all things Competent.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 50],

• and His saying: ﴿And We sent down from the sky blessed water, and We caused to grow thereby gardens and grain for harvest. And tall palm trees with unfolded spathes, provision for the servants, and We gave life thereby to a dead land.﴾ [Qaf: 9–11], then He explained that this is among the proofs of resurrection

• by His saying: ﴿Thus will be the emergence.﴾ [Qaf: 11], i.e., (p-295) your emergence from your graves alive after death,

• as in His saying: ﴿And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He gives life to the earth after its death; and thus you will be brought forth.﴾ [Ar-Rum: 19]

• and His saying: ﴿And We gave life thereby to a dead land.﴾ [Qaf: 11], ﴿Thus We bring forth the dead that you may remember.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 57]

Examples of this kind are numerous.

* *

Notice.

There are two well-known questions concerning this noble verse:

The first: What is the wisdom in conjoining the present tense in His saying "fa-tusbihu" (فَتُصْبِحُ) to the past tense "anzala" (أنْزَلَ)?

The second question: What is the reason for the nominative (raf') in His saying "fa-tusbihu" (فَتُصْبِحُ) although it follows an interrogative?

As for the answer to the first: the point of the present tense is to convey that the effect of the rain persists over time after time, as you say: "So-and-so bestowed favor upon me in such-and-such a year, so I go out and come in thankful to him." Had you said "fa-ghadawtu wa-ruhtu," it would not have fallen into that place. This is how az-Zamakhshari answered.

What appears to me, and Allah knows best, is that the expression with the present tense conveys the bringing to mind of the state the earth takes on after the descent of rain, whereas the past tense does not convey the continuity of that bringing to mind, because it indicates the cessation of the thing.

As for the nominative in "fa-tusbihu": it is because it is not caused by the seeing which is the locus of the interrogation; rather it is caused by the sending down in His saying "anzala," and the sending down, which is the cause of the earth becoming green in the morning, contains no interrogation. It is known that the fa' after which the present tense is put in the subjunctive (naṣb), if it is removed, it is permissible to make what follows it a conditional response (jaza'). But you cannot say here: "If you see that Allah sent down water from the sky, the earth becomes green," because the seeing has no effect whatsoever on the greening of the earth; rather its cause is the sending down of water, not the seeing of its sending down.

Az-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf in answer to this question: "If you say: why is it nominative and not put in the subjunctive as the answer to the interrogative?"

I say: If it were put in the subjunctive, it would give the opposite of the purpose, because its meaning is affirming the greening, so with the subjunctive it becomes negation of the greening.

Example: you say to your companion: "Do you not see that I have bestowed favor upon you, so that you give thanks?" If you put it in the subjunctive, you are negating his thanks and doubting his neglect; if you make it nominative, you are affirming thanks. This and similar points are what one who is characterized by knowledge in the science of i'rab (إعراب, grammatical inflection) should be eager for, and for honoring its people. End of quotation. Abu Hayyan mentioned something similar in al-Bahr, thinking he had clarified it, but it does not appear to me fully clear. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

If it is said: How did He say "fa-tusbihu" when the greening of the earth may come later than the morning of the rain?

The answer: According to the view of one who said "fa-tusbihu al-ardu muhdarratan," meaning "becomes green," the matter is clear, and the Arabs say "aṣbaḥa fulanun ghaniyyan" (أصْبَحَ فُلانٌ غَنِيًّا) meaning "became rich." Abu Hayyan mentioned from some scholars that in some lands the earth becomes green on the very morning of the rain. Ikrimah, Ibn ʿAtiyyah and ʿAli mentioned this, so there is no difficulty. Some said: the fa' indicates sequence (taʿqib), and the sequence of each thing is according to its nature, as in His saying: ﴿Then We made the drop a clinging clot, then We made the clot a lump of flesh﴾ [al-Muminun: 14], even though between these there are forty days as in the hadith; this was said by Ibn Kathir.

As for His saying "Lattifun Khabir" (لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ), it means: Subtle toward His servants; and of His subtlety toward them is that He sends down rain and causes to grow for them through it their sustenance; Acquainted with everything, nothing escapes His knowledge, not even the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, glory be to Him, exalted far above what they say.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 22, verse 65:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is on the earth and the ships that sail through the sea by His command?﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that Allah has subjected to His creation whatever is on the earth, and has subjected to them the ships that run through the sea by His command. What He mentions here has been clarified in many other places, such as His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13]. We have already explained the meaning of the subjugation of what is in the sky in detail in Surah "al-Hijr," in the discussion of His saying: ﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil﴾ [al-Hijr: 17]. And (it is clarified) in His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them from its likeness that which they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-42]. We have clarified the verses indicating this in Surah "al-Nahl" and elsewhere.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾. In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that it is He who holds back the sky and prevents it from falling upon the earth, which would destroy those upon it, and that if He willed, He would permit the sky to fall upon the earth and destroy those on it. As He said: ﴿If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We drop upon them fragments from the sky﴾ [Saba': 9], and He has alluded to this meaning in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41], (p-297) and His saying: ﴿And We have created above you seven heavens, and We are never unaware of creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 17], according to the view of those who interpreted it as meaning: He is not unaware of creation, but rather He protects them from the fall of the heavens, which are expressed by the "paths," upon them.

Note.

These verses mentioned and similar ones in the Qur'an, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth﴾ [al-Hajj: 65]

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41]

• And His saying: ﴿If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them, or We drop upon them fragments from the sky﴾ [Saba': 9]

• And His saying: ﴿And We have built above you seven strong ones﴾ [al-Naba': 12]

• And His saying: ﴿And the sky We built with strength, and indeed, We are expanding it﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ [al-Anbiya': 32]

and the like of these verses, clearly indicate that what the heretical disbelievers claim, and those who follow them from among the blinded of insight who claim to be Muslims, that the sky is merely empty space and not a built solid body, is disbelief, atheism, and zandaqa (heresy), and a denial of the texts of the Mighty Qur'an. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah is, toward mankind, Kind and Merciful﴾ [al-Hajj: 65], meaning: and from His compassion and mercy toward His creation is that He held back the sky from them and did not drop it upon them.

**The Almighty's words: ﴿It is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then will bring you to life again. Indeed, man is ungrateful.﴾ His words: ﴿It is He who gave you life﴾, i.e., after you were dead in the wombs of your mothers before the breath of life was blown into you. So these are two givings of life and two causings of death, as He explained by His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then bring you to life again, then to Him you will be returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], and His saying: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and gave us life twice"﴾, the verse [Ghafir: 11].**

**The counterpart of this verse of al-Hajj (22:66) is His saying in al-Jathiyah: ﴿Say, "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 26]. The disbelief of man mentioned in this verse in His saying ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, despite Allah having given him life twice and caused him to die twice, is what the Qur'an indicated as his obstinacy and denial. Along with the indication of the two deaths and the two lives is the obligation of faith in the One who gives life and causes death, and the impermissibility of disbelieving in Him, in His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 28].(p-٢٩٨)**

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak) which they perform﴾. The most apparent meaning of His words ﴿mansakan hum nasikūhu﴾ [al-Hajj: 67] is: "a form of worship which they perform therein," because the origin of nusk (rite, devotion) is ta'abbud (worship). Allah, exalted is He, has made clear that the rite (mansak) of every community includes drawing near to Allah through sacrifice (dhabh). This is one of the individual forms of nusk, and the Qur'an has explicitly stated that it is included in its general scope. This is one of the kinds of clarification (bayan) which this blessed Book contains.

The verse in which Allah makes this clear is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for every community We have appointed a rite, that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beasts of cattle. For your God is one God, so to Him submit﴾ [al-Hajj: 34]. And His saying ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite﴾ [22:34 and 22:67] in both places was read by Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with a kasra on the sin (mansik), while the rest read it with a fatha on it.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And invite to your Lord; indeed, you are upon right guidance﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, majestic and exalted is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to invite people to their Lord, that is, to His obedience, and informed him that he is upon a straight path (sirat mustaqim), that is, a clear true way with no crookedness in it, which is the religion of Islam, to which he was commanded to invite people. The two matters mentioned in this noble verse have come clearly in other places, such as:

• His saying in the first of them: ﴿And let them not avert you from the signs of Allah after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord, and never be among the polytheists﴾ [al-Qasas: 87].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you have been commanded﴾ [al-Shura: 15].

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]. Allah, majestic and exalted is He, informed that he carried out the command of inviting them to their Lord in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you invite them to a straight path﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 73].

• And His saying: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

• And as in His saying in the last of them: ﴿So rely upon Allah; indeed, you are upon the clear truth﴾ [al-Naml: 79].

• And His saying: ﴿Then We put you on a [clear] course of affair, so follow it﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 18].

• And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And guide you to a straight path﴾ [al-Fath: 2].

Verses of this kind are many.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 68:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they dispute with you, then say: "Allah knows best what you are doing."﴾ Allah, glory be to Him, commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) in this noble verse that if the disbelievers disputed with him, that is, quarrelled with him in falsehood and denied him, he should say to them: "Allah knows best what you are doing."

This statement which he was commanded to make is a threat to them. This verse contains two commands:

The first: The Messenger (ﷺ) was commanded to threaten them with his saying: ﴿Allah knows best what you are doing﴾, that is, of disbelief, so He will recompense you for it with the most severe recompense.

The second: turning away from them. Allah, exalted is He, has indicated the two matters contained in this verse in other places.

As for his turning away from them when they denied him with futile disputation, among the passages in which this is indicated is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they deny you, then say: "For me is my work, and for you is your work. You are free from what I do, and I am free from what you do."﴾ [Yunus: 41]

As for their threat, it has been indicated in several places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿He knows best what you pursue therein. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 8]

• And His saying: ﴿But if they deny you, say: "Your Lord is the Possessor of vast mercy, yet His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people."﴾ [al-An'am: 147] His saying ﴿and His punishment will not be averted﴾ to the end of the verse contains the most severe warning to those who deny, as He said ﴿Woe on that day to the deniers﴾ [al-Mursalat: 15] in many places. They deny him only through disputation and contention in falsehood. Allah had commanded him in another place to dispute with them in the best manner, and that is in His saying: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]

• And His saying: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46]. He made clear to him that they will not bring him any example to argue against him with falsehood, except that Allah brings him the truth which crushes that falsehood, along with it being the better in interpretation, clarification and elucidation of realities. That is in His saying: ﴿And they will not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾ [al-Furqan: 33].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure﴾, meaning: they did not magnify Him with His true magnificence when they worshipped alongside Him those who have no power to create a fly, and who are powerless to retrieve from a fly what the fly has taken from them, such as the perfume they put on their idols. If a fly takes anything from them, the idols cannot rescue it from the fly. Their failure to magnify God with His true magnificence, and their failure to know Him with true knowledge, is evident in that they worshipped alongside Him those who cannot bring about any benefit or ward off any harm. He, exalted is He, mentioned this in other places, such as His saying in al-An'am: ﴿And they did not measure God with His true measure when they said, "God has not sent down anything upon any human being."﴾ [al-An'am: 91], and His saying in az-Zumar: ﴿And they did not measure God with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate.﴾ [az-Zumar: 67].

(p-300) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴿. In this noble verse Allah, may He be majestic and exalted, makes clear that He chooses, that is, selects, messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. So the messengers of mankind are for conveying the revelation, and the messengers of the angels are likewise for that, though He may also send them for other purposes. What He mentions here about His choosing messengers from both categories has been stated clearly in other places, such as His saying about the angelic messengers: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, who makes the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four﴾ [Fatir: 1], and so on.

• And His saying about Jibril: ﴿Indeed, it is the word of a noble messenger﴾ [At-Takwir: 19]. And from His mention of sending angels other than for revelation is His saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him, and they do not neglect﴾ [Al-An'am: 61].

• And like His saying about the messengers of the children of Adam: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [Al-An'am: 124].

• And His saying: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 253], and the verse,

• And His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ [An-Nahl: 36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 22, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has chosen you﴾, i.e., He has selected and preferred you, O nation of Muhammad. The meaning of this verse He clarified with His saying ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110], and so on.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾. Haraj (hardship, constriction) means narrowness, as we explained at the beginning of Surat al-A'raf.

In this noble verse, He has made clear that this upright, tolerant monotheism (hanifiyyah samhah) which our master Muhammad ﷺ brought is founded upon facilitation and ease, not upon narrowness and hardship. In it, Allah has lifted the burdens (aṣar) and the shackles (aghlal) that were upon those before us.

This meaning contained in this noble verse He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentioned in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 185], and His saying: ﴿Allah wishes to lighten for you, and man was created weak﴾ [An-Nisa: 28]. It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Ibn 'Abbas, that when the Prophet ﷺ recited the final verses of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make mistakes﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286], Allah said: "I have done so," in the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, and in the narration of Abu Hurayrah He said: "Yes." Among the lifting of hardship in this sharia is the concession of shortening the prayer during travel, breaking the fast in Ramadan during it, the prayer of one unable to stand, who may pray seated, and the permissibility of what is forbidden out of necessity; as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to﴾ [Al-An'am: 119], and other kinds of facilitation and ease. What this noble verse and the verses we mentioned alongside it contain of lifting hardship and facilitation in the sharia of our Prophet ﷺ is one of the five general legal maxims (al-qawa'id al-khamsah) upon which Islamic jurisprudence (al-fiqh al-Islami) is built, and these are the five:

The first: harm is to be removed (al-darar yuzal). Among its evidences is the hadith: "There is no harm and no reciprocating harm."

The second: hardship brings facilitation (al-mashaqqah tajlib al-taysir). This is what His saying here indicates: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78], along with the verses we mentioned in its meaning.

The third: certainty is not lifted by doubt (la yurfa'u yaqin bi-shakk). Among its evidences is the hadith: "Whoever senses something in his rear during prayer, and it is uncertain whether he has passed wind, should not cut off the prayer until he hears a sound or smells a smell"; because that established purity is not nullified by that doubtful wind.

The fourth: the customs (urf) of people that are current among them in the wording of their contracts and transactions, and the like, are to be applied. Some scholars have cited for this His saying: ﴿And enjoin what is customary﴾ [Al-A'raf: 199], and so on.

The fifth: matters follow their objectives (al-umur tabi' al-maqasid). The evidence for this is the hadith: "Actions are only by intentions," and so on.

In Maraqi al-Su'ud, in the Book of Evidences (kitab al-istidlal), he alluded to these five mentioned with his saying:

Jurisprudence has been founded upon the removal of harm, and that what causes hardship brings about the desired ease.
And he negated the lifting of certainty by doubt, and that custom is to be judged, and he added what the discerning one perceives.
That matters follow objectives, along with some strained inclusion of certain incoming texts.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾. Some said: it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, and Ibn Jarir inclined to this: i.e., He has not placed in your religion any narrowness, like the religion of Ibrahim. Some parsed it as accusative by an implied verb, i.e.: adhere to the religion of your father Ibrahim. It is not far-fetched that His saying ﴿the religion of your father Ibrahim﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78] includes what was mentioned before it of commands in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed﴾ and ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾ [Al-Hajj: 77-78]. This is clarified by His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a correct religion, the religion of Ibrahim, inclining (hanifan)﴾ [Al-An'am: 161]. The upright religion which is the religion of Ibrahim includes all that was mentioned.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He named you Muslims before, and in this﴾. Scholars differed about the referent of the pronoun "He" in His saying ﴿He named you﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78]. Some said: Allah is the One who named you Muslims before, and in this (the Qur'an). This view is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Qatadah said likewise, as Ibn Kathir transmitted from them. Others said: it refers to Ibrahim, who named you Muslims, and they cited the supplication of Ibrahim and Isma'il: ﴿And from our descendants a Muslim nation to You﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 128]. This was also said by 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, as Ibn Kathir transmitted from him.

We have already stated that among the kinds of clarification contained in this blessed book is that some scholars say a view regarding a verse while the verse contains an indication showing that this view is not correct. We brought many examples in the translation and earlier in this book. In these verses there are two indications showing that the view of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam is not correct.

The first: Allah said ﴿He named you Muslims before, and in this﴾, i.e., in the Qur'an, and it is known that Ibrahim did not name them Muslims in the Qur'an, since it was revealed many long years after his death, as Ibn Jarir pointed out.

The second indication: all the verbs in the mentioned context refer back to Allah, not to Ibrahim. So His saying ﴿He has chosen you﴾, i.e., Allah, and ﴿and He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾, i.e., Allah, and ﴿He named you Muslims﴾, i.e., Allah.

If it is said: the pronoun returns to the nearest preceding referent, and the nearest preceding referent for the pronoun is Ibrahim.

The answer: the place where a pronoun returns to the nearest referent applies only when no diverting factor turns it away; here a diverting factor has turned it away, because His saying "and in this" meaning the Qur'an, is evidence that the one who named them Muslims in it is Allah and not Ibrahim. Likewise the context of the sentences before it, such as ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾ [Al-Hajj: 78], fits that He is the one who named you, i.e., Allah, Muslims.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on the verse, after mentioning that the One who named them Muslims before and in this is Allah, not Ibrahim, the following text:

I say: this is the correct view, because He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾, then He urged and encouraged them upon what the Messenger ﷺ brought, saying it is the religion of Ibrahim, their father the Friend (Khalil), then He mentioned His favor upon this nation by what He had made known of its mention and praise in ancient times and former ages in the books of the prophets, recited to the rabbis and monks, and He said: ﴿He named you Muslims before﴾, i.e., before this Qur'an.

Regarding this, al-Nasa'i narrated at the commentary of this verse: Hisham ibn 'Ammar informed us, Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb informed us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salam informed us that his brother Zayd ibn Salam informed him, from Abu Salam, that he informed him, saying: al-Harith al-Ash'ari informed me, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Whoever calls with the call of the Jahiliyyah, he is among the kneeling ones (juthiyy) of Hell." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if he fasts and prays?" He said: "Yes, even if he fasts and prays. So call with the call of Allah with which He named you Muslims, believers, servants of Allah." We have already mentioned this hadith in full at the commentary of His saying: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord who created you and those before you that you may become righteous﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 21]. End of Ibn Kathir's commentary.

Ibn Kathir also said in his commentary on Surat al-Baqarah that the hadith mentioned therein indicates that Allah is the One who named them Muslims, the believers.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That the Messenger may be a witness over you and that you may be witnesses over mankind﴾. He means: He chose you, favored you, and made your name "Muslims" известным before the revelation of your Book, and purified you through the tongues of the earlier messengers, so He named you Muslims in their books, and likewise He named you in this Qur'an. Thereby it is known that you are a middle nation (ummah wasat), upright, choice, whose uprightness is attested, so that you may be witnesses over mankind on the Day of Resurrection, that the messengers conveyed the messages of their Lord, when the disbelievers deny that on the Day of Resurrection; and the Messenger will be a witness over you, that he conveyed to you. It was also said: a witness upon your truthfulness regarding what you testify to the messengers concerning the conveying by them to their peoples.

This meaning mentioned here, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, mentioned in His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143]. And He said of him ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you as a witness﴾ [Al-Fath: 8]. And Allah knows best.
